Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 One turn per user request, with a server-issued request token. Every user message that reaches a host arrival mechanism (prompt hook, arrival bridge, or host-native hook adapter; D5, D6) maps to exactly one session-log turn whose `requestId` the server mints at ingress (operator D1).

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC001 The plugin opens every turn through the server mint operation (`POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint` with an `ingressNonce`, or its client and REPL equivalents, called only by hooks and adapters); the server mints `req-<server UTC yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 lowercase hex random>`, opens the turn `in_progress`, and returns the token; the plugin never invents a requestId. The plugin's `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` verb is retired: no tool descriptor names it, and a call is refused with `mint_requires_host_ingress` before any server call (architecture 4.1; `repl-invoke.ps1:2161,3047` at `a8d3934b`; `BeginTurnVerbRetiredRefusedMintRequiresHostIngress`). A minted requestId is unique within the workspace, enforced by the database for minted turns across all sessions; a violation of that requestId index makes the server generate a new requestId (at most 5 retries after the original attempt, 6 attempts in all, then 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`) and never merges into another turn, while a violation of the nonce index means the same event and returns the existing requestId (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC002) (`MinterCollisionReturnsDistinctId`, `MintCollisionConcurrentCrossSessionDistinctIds` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server). The mint is a single-turn write under turn-level isolation (architecture 3.1, "Mint isolation", and 4.2, MintSessionTurnCommand): it reads and writes only its session row and the one turn it inserts, so a mint never conflicts with a write to another turn of the same session (`MintConcurrentWithOtherTurnWriteSameSessionBothCommitNoConflictAnswer`); the six-attempt bound covers request-id collisions only, and a transient conflict (SQL Server 1205, PostgreSQL 40001 and 40P01, SQLite 5 and 6) uses SerializableWrite's four attempts and then answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing (`MintTransientConflictFourAttempts409ConflictRetryableNothingSaved`, three providers), which the plugin handles as an outage (AC008). [A1 server, A3 plugin]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC002 Repeating the mint with the same agent, MCP session id, and `ingressNonce` (network retry, two hook processes started for one event, or failsafe replay after an outage) returns the same requestId and opens no second turn (server behavior on every host; on copilot and classic cline the hook applies the equal-field rule to a `merged` result of a new invocation, so it fails the host session closed instead of binding, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain binds normally). A same-nonce mint for a turn that is already terminal returns `merged` with that `storedStatus`, leaves the status unchanged, and the hook neither makes it the write target nor adds it to the open list or the stop ledger (`MintSameNonceTerminalTurnMergedNotReopened` server side; `PromptHookSameNonceTerminalTurnMergedNotTargetNotOpenNotLedger` plugin side). A prompt hook killed at any point after its write-ahead mint record (before the mint call, after the server committed the mint, or before its delivery replace) ends at the next hook, verb, or SessionStart drain with exactly one server turn for that message, delivered once: the drain's mint with the same nonce returns the stored turn, which enters the open list and the ledger and becomes the write target only when no later request was delivered in that host session, and a merged terminal turn is never delivered (architecture 3.1 and 4.4, DrainFailsafe "Delivery once"; what-if W-4; `PromptHookKilledAfterServerMintBeforeDeliveryNextDrainOneTurnDeliveredOnce`). [A1 server, A3 plugin, A4 plugin write target, open list, ledger, and killed-hook delivery]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC003 Two user messages with identical prompt text (an intentional repeat, at any interval; on copilot and classic cline the equal-field rule governs a repeat that also shares the timestamp) are two events, derive two nonces, and receive two requestIds and two turns; two independent hook processes receiving one event (a doubly registered hook) derive one nonce from the host binding table and receive one requestId on every host whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex, grok, grok-bot, cline-v2, opencode; cline-v2 is supported only when P0.2 shows one run per user message, otherwise D6, architecture 3.1; on bridge hosts the single bridge per host session mints, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-006); on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint (D11 and the classic-cline single-registration check), so the positive two-process case does not apply there. On copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id, two messages whose timestamps differ mint two turns, a second new invocation with equal session, timestamp, and prompt cannot be told apart from a separate message, so it mints nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 (`indistinguishable_arrival`) rather than merging or guessing, and a retry or failsafe replay of one stored mint reuses its nonce (`CopilotSamePromptDifferentTimestampTwoMints`, `CopilotEqualFieldsSecondInvocationFailsClosedNoSecondMint`, `CopilotMintRetryAndFailsafeReplayReuseNonceNoFailClose`, `ClineSamePromptDifferentTimestampTwoMints`, `ClineEqualFieldsSecondInvocationFailsClosedNoSecondMint`, `ClineMintRetryAndFailsafeReplayReuseNonceNoFailClose`). [A1 server, A3 plugin, A8 TypeScript hosts +A4 +A9]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC004 Distinct prompts open distinct turns, and on every prompt-hook and adapter host whose P0.2 row passed, each prompt form of AC009 that the host delivers to its hook (including a prompt of at least 1 MiB, non-ASCII, CRLF, and image-only) mints exactly one turn (what-if W-11; `PromptHookPromptFormsOneMintEachPerHost`; on the TypeScript hosts through the PowerShell core, `TsHostPromptFormsOneMintEach`). [A3 +A8]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC005 A message delivered while another turn is in progress (queued or mid-turn) gets its own turn, minted by the host's arrival mechanism (arrival bridge, prompt hook, or host-native hook adapter); the running turn is not changed. [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC006 The Claude hook validator reports `duplicate` when an MCP hook script is registered by both `~/.claude/settings.json` and the enabled plugin, repairs it with a backup, and `-CheckOnly` never mutates settings; when the backup cannot be written, no settings file changes and the validator reports the failure (architecture 4.4, ValidateHookRegistration; what-if W-25; `RepairBackupWriteFailsNoSettingsChangeReportsFailure`). [A2]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC007 The hook installer adds no bridge hook for an event the enabled plugin already covers. [A2]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 When the server is unreachable at ingress, the hook persists a failsafe mint record carrying its nonce and opens a provisional local turn `pending-<nonce>`; on failsafe drain the server mints idempotently from the nonce and the plugin rebinds the provisional turn and every write bound to it to the minted requestId, in original order. Either id resolves to the same turn; a crash at any point during the rebind loses no write and creates no second turn; a committed pending-to-minted alias stays discoverable and is reapplied until every consumer of it (including an audit outbox) durably acknowledges it, and duplicate delivery or application is harmless (C2). With two or more consumers, an alias acknowledged by one stays discoverable to the others; replay to a consumer stops only after that consumer durably acknowledges, and stops entirely once all have. No server turn ever has a `pending-` requestId: a write captured under a pending id and sent after the alias is sent under the minted id, and the writes of one turn reach the server in their original order even when a close of that turn was made while earlier writes waited in the failsafe. A mint that the server or REPL does not support is recognized only by the trusted mint adapter (A3, in the PowerShell core) for the exact mint operation, from either an authenticated, bound mint-endpoint response with HTTP 404 and no detail code, or the structured `unknown_method` (GenericClientPassthrough) or `method_not_found` (ReplCommandDispatcher) result for the expected mint verb, as on a server older than A1; it is never inferred from prose, malformed detail metadata, arbitrary 404s, or unrelated operations, keeps the original structured cause, and is classified as a transport outage by that adapter only (never by the generic C9 classifier or the audit outbox in-call retry loop) and handled like one (failsafe retained, turn stays `pending-<nonce>`, retried at a later drain). `Resolve-MintOutcome` (architecture 3.5.6, in `plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1`) is the one classifier of a mint answer for the prompt hook, the arrival bridge, and the drain: a transport outage, a retryable 503 (`backend_unavailable`, or a busy store's `persistence_error` with `retryable: true`), 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, the scoped mint 404 or `unknown_method` above, and `session_not_open` while the session open for the record's envelope is not confirmed are outages (`MintRetryable409Or503OutagePendingIdFailsafeRecordKept`); a mint refused for a final reason (`ingress_nonce_invalid`, `validation_error` including an unresolved workspace's 400 with `details.field` `workspacePath`, `mint_collision_exhausted`, or `session_not_open` after a confirmed session open) reports `turn-open-failed` with the server code and invents no requestId; on the prompt hook its write-ahead mint record counts that answer as its first drain attempt (`drainAttempts` 1), the drain mints it again under the attempt budget of 5, each final answer counting one more, and then moves it to the quarantine subdirectory with its `.reason.txt` (architecture 3.1, "Failsafe drain"; `PromptHookFinalMintRefusalRecordKeptDrainAttemptsOne`; the budget and quarantine cases are the persistence domain's drain cases); on the bridge it becomes an `open-failed` queue entry that the bridge never mints again (AC010); and the stop gate warns naming the prompt while the record is queued or quarantined (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC005). A verb whose bound id is a `pending-<nonce>` id, or whose host session's failsafe holds drainable records, first runs the drain; when the pending id still has no journaled alias, or a record of the bound turn stays queued, the write is captured in the failsafe behind them (`queued`) and is never sent under the pending id, on the submit, dialog, and title routes (architecture 4.4, PersistTurnWriteWithReceipt; what-if W-10; `PendingTargetServerReachableVerbDrainsMintFirstNeverSendsPendingIdAllRoutes`). On drain the plugin first replays an idempotent session open for the record's envelope `mcpSessionId` (an outage that spanned SessionStart left that session unopened on the server), then the mint; a `session_not_open` refusal is final only after that session open is confirmed (`OutageSpanningSessionStartDrainOpensSessionThenMintsNotFinal`). The pending-to-minted lookup entry is permanent for the life of the plugin cache: retiring an alias's consumer-delivery obligation after the last required acknowledgement never removes it, so a reader holding the pending id resolves the minted turn after every acknowledgement and after a restart. After the delivery obligation is retired, `getAlias` still returns the full agreed record with the exact final acknowledgement set, and a repeated acknowledgement is an idempotent no-op. [A3 +A5 +A8]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009 Arrival bridge (D5): on claude-code, and on claude-cowork when P0.2 shows Cowork runs plugin hooks and passes the same bridge probes as claude-code (otherwise FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC004 applies: Cowork reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and the feature matrix records the limitation), the arrival bridge is the only minter: every user message is minted from its transcript `enqueue` record (nonce `q-` from that record) before the model processes it, in state `queued`, and the prompt hook neither mints nor claims (in `Pilot` or `Stateless` it applies pending records through `Sync-PluginArrivalLog` and takes the bridge-minted requestId, still minting nothing; architecture 4.4, ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord, specified under FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009), so no hook-to-bridge correlation exists to fail (Claude Code's `queue-operation` records carry no parent `promptId`; the plan never correlates across record kinds without a shared key). One message yields exactly one mint for every prompt form P0.2 captures (plain, slash command, attachment or image, image-only, multi-line CRLF, non-ASCII, at least 1 MiB), and two messages with equal text yield two mints. A pid file naming a dead or foreign process does not prevent a bridge start; a host session ended by the idle rule (`ended.yaml` with `reason: idle`) is live again at its next mint or keyed verb from that host session key, which removes the marker in the same atomic replace under `turn-open.lock` before acting; a keyed verb that revives a session with no delivered request is then refused with `request_unknown` (no write target); a `reason: session_end` marker is revived only by a SessionStart for the same host session key (Claude Code resume and `codex exec resume` reuse the key), which removes it in one atomic replace under `turn-open.lock`, as the idle revival does, and continues in the host session's recorded MCP session, because `Invoke-SessionOpen` never replaces a recorded `mcpSessionId`; a keyed verb never revives it (operator, 2026-10-12, verbatim answer "Revive, keep MCP session (Recommended)"; architecture 3.1 and 4.4, StartHostSession and EndHostSession) (`IdleEndedKeyedVerbRevivesAtomicallyNoTargetRequestUnknown`, `IdleEndedRevivalCrashRestartConsistent`, `SessionEndMarkerResumeSessionStartRevivesKeepsMcpSessionId`, `SessionEndMarkerKeyedVerbDoesNotRevive`); a resumed or forked transcript mints nothing for queue records written before that host session's SessionStart; a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset` is reported with `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, changes no queue entry, records `unsupportedSince` with that reason after a delivered request (unsupported-session rule), and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported`, with writes for its already open turns going to the plugin failsafe, until the bridge restarts on a valid transcript (fail closed, like an unknown record shape); the bridge restarts from SessionStart after `/clear` and resume; it stops when `ended.yaml` with `reason: session_end` is written for its key, while an idle end does not stop it, so a message enqueued after an idle end is still minted at enqueue (`IdleEndedThenMidTurnMessageMintedAtEnqueue`); and a bridge whose running version differs from the active plugin cache is treated as a stale pid, stopped, and restarted from the active cache with `appliedThroughOffset` kept (architecture 3.1 and 4.4, RunArrivalBridge; FR-MCP-TRIAGEPLUGIN-001; `BridgeRunningOtherCacheVersionRestartedFromActiveCacheOffsetKept`). If P0.2 shows a user prompt that produces no `enqueue` record, a `dequeue` that does not take the head, or a request whose `dequeue` line (or `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`) is not in the transcript before that request's first tool call starts, the host is `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6) (architecture 3.1, "Late `dequeue` on claude-code", which settles what-if W-9; `ClaudeCodeP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`; the real prompt-form fixture case runs only when those probes pass); when they pass, a verb started at a request's first tool call binds to that request on its P0.2-recorded transcript (`BridgeDequeueRecordedBeforeFirstToolCallVerbBindsToDequeuedRequest`). [A3 +A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010 Queue lifecycle: a `queued` request becomes `delivered` (and the host session's write target) at `dequeue` (the head of the queue) or at `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`, and becomes `withdrawn` at a `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason; minting never moves the write target; a withdrawn request stays `in_progress` on the server until the model closes it (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009). A record that cannot be attributed (equal content with no shared key, or a record that matches nothing: a `remove` matching zero or two or more queued entries, or a `popAll` in which, for some content, the line count differs from the number of queued entries of any kind with that content, or that leaves a queued entry unpopped; a `dequeue` with no queue head is an unrecognized format and fails closed with `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`; architecture 4.4, ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord; what-if W-7) is never guessed: the host session fails closed under D6 (the bridge stops before the record, `unsupportedSince` is recorded, every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until it ends, writes for its already open turns go to the plugin failsafe and drain only after that host session ends or a SessionStart clears its cause (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; architecture 4.4, DrainFailsafe), and its open turns are listed with their pairs at the next SessionStart); a `popAll` whose line counts equal the queued entries of every content it carries and that pops every queued entry withdraws every queued request entry in progress and drops every other queued entry. Every `enqueue` takes a queue position: system events as unminted `kind: system` entries, so a `dequeue` whose head is a system entry delivers nothing and the user request behind it stays `queued` until its own delivery (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001). A user `enqueue` whose mint is refused for a final reason becomes a `kind: open-failed` entry with the server code and no requestId, and a request entry whose mint returned `merged` with a terminal `storedStatus` keeps that status; each keeps its queue position, so a later `dequeue`, `remove`, or `popAll` that takes it delivers and withdraws nothing, and the bridge never mints an `open-failed` entry again (the Stop gate's warning naming its prompt is FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC005) (architecture 4.1 request lifecycle and 4.4 ApplyEnqueueRecord, ApplyDequeueRecord, ApplyRemoveRecord; what-if W-8; `BridgeRemoveMatchingNoEntryFailsClosed`, `BridgePopAllExtraLineOrUnpoppedEntryFailsClosed`, `BridgeDequeueEmptyQueueFormatUnrecognizedFailsClosed`, `BridgeFinalMintRefusalOpenFailedKeepsPositionDequeueDeliversNothing`, `BridgeMergedTerminalAtMintKeepsPositionDequeueDeliversNothing`). [A3 +A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002 Background and system events never open turns.

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001 Prompts that are `<task-notification>`, `<local-command-*>`, `<agent-message ...>` subagent hand-backs, or only system-reminder blocks, payloads marking a subagent (Claude Code `agent_id`, Grok `subagentType`), deliveries with `MCP_SUBAGENT_ID`/`GROK_SUBAGENT_ID` set, and a host-local command that never reaches the model (for example `/clear`, `/compact`) when P0.2 shows it produces an arrival event (architecture 3.1; `HostLocalCommandWithArrivalEventSystemEventNoMint`, run on the P0.2-recorded payload where one exists) open no turn, call no mint, leave turn state unchanged, and report `system-event-skipped`; classification uses these structural markers only, never the topic or wording of the prompt. On every supported host a prompt event produced by a subagent or a child session (for example an opencode `task` child session's `chat.message`) opens no turn; P0.2 records each host's subagent marker, and a host without one records the limitation in the feature matrix. On bridge hosts a system-event `enqueue` still occupies a queue position (`kind: system`), so its later `dequeue` or removal never delivers or withdraws a user request (`BridgeSystemEnqueueAheadOfUserSystemDequeueUserStaysQueued`, `BridgeSystemEnqueueRemovedNoTurn`, `BridgeSystemAndUserInterleavedCrashReplayZeroWrongTurnWrites`; the `MCP_SUBAGENT_ID`/`GROK_SUBAGENT_ID` deliveries `SystemEventsSubagentEnvMarkersNoMint`; the opencode child session `OpenCodeChildSessionChatMessageNoTurn`). [A3 +A4 +A8]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC002 Slash-command (`<command-name>`) prompts that reach the model and `<user_query>` prompts open turns (a host-local command is a system event under AC001), and so does any user prompt that happens to contain a hostile-review or delegation brief (for example the brief that launches a Codex hostile reviewer, which needs its own reviewer turn), because the prompt hook classifies a background agent only by the host's subagent markers, never by prompt text; this replaces FR-MCP-TRIAGEPLUGIN-001's text-detected background-brief reuse (`Test-PluginPromptIsBackgroundAgent` and `Get-PluginRootTurnIsolationDecision`, `plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1:693,725` at `a8d3934b`; architecture 5.4 and 7.8) and opens the new turn without changing any other turn (`HostileReviewBriefPromptOpensOwnTurnAgentIdPayloadDoesNot`). [A3]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC003 Hooks of subagents or parallel sessions sharing the workspace cache never change this session's turn state. [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003 A new prompt never cancels an in-progress turn.

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC001 Opening a turn never persists `canceled` for any other turn. [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC002 The prior in-progress turn stays `in_progress` locally and on the server and remains addressable by requestId. [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC003 Only the model closes turns; no hook calls complete or fail. [A7]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC004 The stop ledger lists every request delivered since the last passing Stop, plus every earlier entry whose close the server has not confirmed; a request that is minted but still `queued` is not in it until it is delivered (the single enrollment rule of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001). Only a server-confirmed close leaves the ledger (A5 outcome mapping, `CloseVerbOnlyServerConfirmedCloseLeavesOpenListAndLedger`), and the Stop gate evaluates that ledger plus one separate scan of `withdrawn` queue entries still `in_progress` (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006 AC-005), so a request withdrawn before delivery is blocked as `turn_withdrawn_unclosed` without ever entering the ledger (A7, `StopGateLedgerListsDeliveredSinceLastPassPlusUnconfirmedCloses`, `StopGateWithdrawnBeforeDeliveryEmptyLedgerBlocksWithdrawnUnclosedFailByPairNextStopPasses`). [A4 +A5 +A7]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007 Independent turn edits.

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC001 Each turn has its own state file and lock; each host session has one state file `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml` holding its write target (the request most recently delivered to the model; D9 refuses unqualified writes while several delivered requests are open), its open delivered requests, its queue (minted requests with `queued`/`delivered`/`withdrawn` state), `appliedThroughOffset`, and the host session's own `mcpSessionId`, which StartHostSession (on the TypeScript hosts, which have no SessionStart event, the first ingress event for that host session key, A8) records only when none is recorded for the key, always replaced atomically (temp file, flush, rename) under `turn-open.lock` through `Update-TurnState` (architecture 3.5.6); `current-turn.yaml` remains only as a read-only legacy status file that no verb uses for targeting. The arrival bridge, the mint, and every verb read the MCP session id only from their own host session's turn-state; the workspace-level `session-state.yaml` keeps develop's trust and header fields and is never read for targeting, and the rotated-sessionId rebind (`repl-invoke.ps1:1954-1965` at `a8d3934b`, TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012) is removed, because `Assert-ReplCurrentTurnFresh` keeps only its marker-drift check (architecture 4.1), so a second host session's SessionStart never retargets the first (`TwoHostSessionsOwnMcpSessionIdsSecondSessionStartNeverRetargetsFirst`, TypeScript hosts `TsHostTwoHostSessionsOwnMcpSessionIdsSecondNeverRetargetsFirst`). A later SessionStart, a claude-code PostCompact run (which runs StartHostSession for the same key), or a resumed key for a host session key that already has a recorded `mcpSessionId` keeps it: no new MCP session is opened for that key, its open turns stay bound and close in their original MCP session, no `unsupported_session` record of that still-live host session is drained, and a PostCompact run lists nothing and emits no `additionalContext` (FR-MCP-115, TR-MCP-PLUGIN-009, and TEST-MCP-155 kept) (architecture 3.1, "Compaction and resume", which replaces TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012's rotation rebind; what-if W-3; `PostCompactSameHostSessionKeyKeepsMcpSessionIdOpenTurnClosesInOriginalSession`, `PostCompactUnsupportedSessionCapturedRecordsNotDrained`). StartHostSession first runs develop's trust bootstrap (`Invoke-FullBootstrap` with the marker snapshot, `plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1:286-308` at `a8d3934b`) and agent runtime header capture (`:314-326`, TR-MCP-PLUGIN-HEADER-001) unchanged: an unverified marker records `MCP_UNTRUSTED` in the workspace `session-state.yaml` as today and ends the process before the session open, with no server call; a new `mcpSessionId` comes from develop's `New-PluginSessionId` (`:47-56`), the `MCP_SESSION_ID` override when it is set, else `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`, and host sessions that share an override share one MCP session while each keeps its own `turn-state.yaml` (architecture 3.1, "Host session start state"; C5; `SessionStartUnverifiedMarkerRecordsUntrustedNoSessionOpenNoServerCall`, `SessionStartNewMcpSessionIdFromNewPluginSessionIdOverrideHonored`). A prompt hook whose host session has no recorded `mcpSessionId` (no SessionStart ran for its key) first runs StartHostSession for that key from its own payload (the session key, and on claude-code and claude-cowork the `transcript_path` that starts the bridge; on a host without a SessionStart event, the first-ingress writer), so an unreachable server is then the mint's outage (`turn-opened-degraded`) and the drain opens the session before it mints; this replaces develop's no-session recovery (`Invoke-PluginNoSessionRecovery`, `plugin-hook.ps1:541`, status `no-session` at `:778`; architecture 3.1, "Prompt without a recorded session"; `PromptHookNoRecordedSessionRunsStartHostSessionForKeyThenMints`). The plugin's `openSession` verb resolves its host session as a verb does and opens that host session's recorded `mcpSessionId` through `Invoke-SessionOpen` (OpenSessionLogCommand), writing no `session-state.yaml` (architecture 4.1; `repl-invoke.ps1:243-293` at `a8d3934b` writes only that file today; `OpenSessionVerbOpensOwnHostSessionMcpSessionIdNoSessionStateWrite`). [A4 +A8]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC002 Every verb resolves exactly one target turn, in this precedence: explicit `requestId` override, else the invocation's bound request, which is refused with `request_ambiguous` while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9); it mutates only that turn; an explicit requestId resolves to exactly one immutable owning MCP session within the validated workspace and agent, and naming a turn of an earlier host session requires its original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, used only by recovery and review backfill (C5); an unknown explicit requestId is refused with `request_unknown`, and a terminal one with `turn_immutable` (except the review and class writes allowed on terminal turns, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC004). A verb whose host session has no delivered request (no write target) is refused with `request_unknown` naming the host session key and writes nothing (`BindingNoWriteTargetRequestUnknownNamesHostSessionKey`). With no delivered request open and a write target set, an unqualified verb targets that write target even when it is closed, and every verb other than `recordReview` and a requestClass-only update is refused with `turn_immutable` (architecture 4.4, BindVerbToTurn, "Closed write target"; what-if X-7; `BindingClosedWriteTargetNoOpenRequestOtherVerbsTurnImmutable`; the acceptance of the review and class-only writes is FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC004 and FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002-AC003, from S8). A `request_ambiguous` refusal lists each open delivered request's requestId, delivery time, source, and title. [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC003 Concurrent edits to two turns from separate processes lose nothing and cross-contaminate nothing, and concurrent edits to one turn from separate processes (for example parallel `appendActions` and `appendDecisions`, serialized locally by that turn's own lock `turns/<requestId>.lock`, architecture 3.4) lose no item locally or on the server (what-if W-14; `ConcurrentEditsSameTurnTwoProcessesNoLostItem`). [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC004 Failsafe records and fingerprints are namespaced by requestId; replay never targets another turn. A failsafe record without a captured binding (written before the upgrade) is never bound to a turn by any later binding: on every drain trigger (SessionStart, the next hook or verb, and the explicit `workflow.failsafe.drain` verb) a record that names no request (it relied on `current-turn.yaml`) moves to the quarantine subdirectory with its `.reason.txt`, and a record whose parameters name its session and request replays its method and parameters onto that turn as today (architecture 3.1, "Failsafe drain", and 4.4, DrainOneFailsafeRecord; what-if W-27); a turn in progress in the legacy `current-turn.yaml` at upgrade is listed with its pair by the first SessionStart, warned by the Stop gate, and stays addressable by explicit requestId (`FailsafeLegacyNoRequestQuarantinedOnEveryDrainTrigger`, `FailsafeLegacyNamingSessionAndRequestReplaysOwnTurnOnly`, `LegacyCurrentTurnInProgressListedAtFirstSessionStartAddressableByRequestId` in A4; the Stop warning `StopGateLegacyCurrentTurnInProgressWarned` in A7). [A4 +A7]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC005 Opening, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn locally or on the server. [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC006 Host-context binding (operator D2): at the start of each verb invocation the plugin resolves the invoking host session's key by the host's locked method (see the host binding table) and binds the invocation to that host session's write target; the binding is written into the invocation's persist and failsafe records and never re-resolved, so a prompt minted after the invocation started never retargets it. On hosts with an arrival bridge, the invocation records the transcript length when it starts and then applies, under `turn-open.lock`, exactly the transcript records that end at or before that length (records appended after it started are left for later invocations), so the binding is the invocation-start snapshot D2 requires and reflects every delivery recorded before the invocation began. A hook payload (prompt, SessionStart, PostCompact, or SessionEnd) without the host row's session key refuses with `host_session_unknown` and writes nothing; the live-session rule applies only to verbs (architecture 3.1, which settles what-if Q-12, and 4.4, OpenTurnFromPromptHook and StartHostSession; `HookPayloadWithoutHostSessionKeyRefusedNothingWritten`; the Stop hook's same refusal is FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005's, architecture 4.4 EvaluateStopGate). The `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -Command CompleteTurn` entry (`plugins/core/lib-ps/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1:344-351`, `plugins/core/lib-ps/final-response.ps1:27` at `a8d3934b`) is the `completeTurn` verb: process BindVerbToTurn binds it from its invocation context like every verb, and it carries no evidence of its own, so its close passes `Test-ModelEvidence` and `Get-CloseRemedy` like any close (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002) (architecture 3.1, "`final-response.ps1`"; `FinalResponseCompleteTurnEntryBoundLikeVerbNoEvidenceRefusedWithRemedy`). [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC007 Interleaving: with R1 delivered and R2 enqueued mid-turn in the same host session, a verb started after R2's mint but before R2's delivery (`absorbed_mid_turn` or `dequeue`) writes to R1; a verb started after R2's delivery without `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous` while R1 and R2 are both open (D9); with explicit ids an R1, R2, R1 sequence of writes lands on R1, R2, R1 respectively; once R1 is closed an unqualified verb writes to R2; a withdrawn R2 never becomes a write target; R1 stays in progress throughout. When the verb cannot read its host session key, the live-session rule applies: with exactly one live host session of its agent it binds there with warning `host_session_inferred`; with none or several it is refused (`host_session_unknown`, `host_session_ambiguous`) unless it carries the trusted (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair of C5 that the server verifies for this workspace and agent; a `requestId` alone is refused the same way; with two concurrent host sessions in one workspace and no keys, zero writes land on the wrong turn. After a prompt's open fails (`turn-open-contended`, `turn-open-failed`, `nonce_source_missing`), unqualified verbs in that host session are refused with `request_unknown` until a later delivery succeeds, so that prompt's work never lands on the earlier turn (`BindingAfterFailedOpenUnqualifiedVerbRequestUnknown`). A turn the server reports terminal, whichever surface closed it, stops counting as an open delivered request at the next verb or Stop, and a request leaves the open list only when the server confirms its close (a queued, refused, or failed close leaves it open; A5 outcome mapping `CloseVerbOnlyServerConfirmedCloseLeavesOpenListAndLedger`, A7 Stop `StopGateTurnClosedElsewhereDroppedFromOpenList`). When the write target is closed while an earlier delivered request is still open, an unqualified verb other than `recordReview` and a requestClass-only update is refused with `turn_immutable` naming the open request (architecture 4.4, BindVerbToTurn, "Closed write target"; `BindingWriteTargetClosedEarlierStillOpenTurnImmutable`). [A4 +A5 +A7]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC008 Session changes in place never misattribute: after Claude Code `/clear`, a shell verb binds to the new session's write target (its `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is updated), a long-lived process resolves per call by the live-session rule (the cleared session is ended by SessionEnd reason `clear`), and after resume the resumed session's key is used; a resumed key whose `ended.yaml` says `session_end` is revived by its SessionStart and keeps its recorded MCP session (AC001, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009; `SessionEndMarkerResumeSessionStartRevivesKeepsMcpSessionId`). [A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC009 Every record family the plugins write for a turn (queue entry, alias, failsafe record, stop-ledger entry inside `turn-state.yaml`, persisted or queued event) carries the root-id envelope `{ workspacePath, agent, mcpSessionId, hostSessionKey, ingressNonce, requestId }` (`requestId` may be the pending alias until rebind), while a session-scoped record that belongs to no turn (a `kind: system` queue entry, `unsupportedSince`) carries the session-level envelope `{ workspacePath, agent, mcpSessionId, hostSessionKey }` plus its own key (`enqueueOffset`, `causeOffset`, on a prompt-hook host `causeNonce`, or, for a cause with neither, its `reason` and `detectedAtUtc`), never an invented nonce or requestId, so each record is attributable on its own without consulting another record (operator, 2026-10-09: "The root id of whatever something is a child of or depends on, should always be carried."; design principle: "Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities."); each family is read back after write and after replay with the envelope intact (`RootIdsEveryRecordFamilyPresentAfterWriteAndReplay`, including the alias). [A3 +A4]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 Turn-open lock, ingress mint client, system-event classifier (lib-ps). AC-001 `turn-open.lock` serializes opens across processes in one workspace cache; it is taken only through `Update-TurnState` (architecture 3.5.6), and the prompt hook takes it once and never waits: a contended open reports `turn-open-contended`, writes the same failsafe diagnostic as `nonce_source_missing` naming the prompt, invents no nonce, and mints nothing (architecture 3.1 and 4.4, OpenTurnFromPromptHook; what-if W-5; `ContendedTurnOpenLockReportsTurnOpenContendedNoMint`, `ContendedTurnOpenLockDiagnosticWrittenNamingPrompt`; the Stop warning is FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC005's); a process that dies while holding the lock never blocks a later acquirer, and its change is either fully applied or absent, as the atomic replace guarantees (what-if W-6; `TurnOpenLockHolderKilledNextAcquirerProceedsStateConsistent`); AC-002 `Get-PluginIngressNonce -Host <host> -Payload <payload>` derives the nonce from the event exactly as the host binding table states for each hook host (a pure function: equal payloads give equal nonces), and when a payload lacks the field its host row names, the hook does not invent a nonce: it reports `turn-open-failed` with reason `nonce_source_missing` and writes a failsafe diagnostic, which the stop gate shows as warning `nonce_source_missing`; the nonce is written into the failsafe mint record before the first mint call, and the host binding table equal-field rule is applied under `turn-open.lock` before that write (`indistinguishable_arrival`); the arrival bridge keeps no write-ahead mint record, because the transcript is its durable source (architecture 4.4, ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord; what-if X-3); AC-003 classifier returns true exactly for the FR-002 event list; AC-004 hook-originated verbs carry `MCP_PLUGIN_HOOK_INVOCATION=1`; AC-005 `Invoke-PluginIngressMint` calls the server mint with the nonce through the REPL verb `workflow.sessionlog.mintTurn`, statelessly with explicit agent, sessionId, and nonce, and classifies the answer through `Resolve-MintOutcome` (architecture 3.5.6: the one classifier for the prompt hook, the arrival bridge, and the drain, in `plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1`, the dot-sourceable library that `plugin-hook.ps1` dot-sources, architecture 3.1, "Plugin function home"); the verb's response carries the FR-MCP-REPL-006 deprecation marker that the dispatcher puts on every `workflow.*` response (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/ReplCommandDispatcher.cs:212-222,330` at `a8d3934b`) and that `Resolve-MintOutcome` ignores when it maps the result (what-if W-26; `MintTurnReplDeprecationMarkerIgnoredByCore`); the mint client records the returned requestId (a prompt-hook mint is delivered at once, so it also becomes the host session's write target; a bridge mint stays `queued` until delivery), and on outage opens `pending-<nonce>` and rebinds it on drain through the C2 alias journal `sessions/<key>/aliases.yaml` (one atomic replace adding `{ pendingId, requestId, aliasedAtUtc } plus the root-id envelope of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC009` before any queued record is rewritten; readers resolve either id through it; replay reapplies a journaled alias without minting); AC-006 `Start-PluginArrivalBridge` (claude-code, claude-cowork) is launched by SessionStart (process RunArrivalBridge) as a detached `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive` process of the bridge's own script entry in `plugins/core/lib-ps`, which dot-sources `repl-invoke.ps1` for the section 3.5.6 functions (architecture 3.1, "Plugin function home"), with the workspace root as working directory, writes `sessions/<key>/arrival-bridge.pid`, tails `transcript_path` from `appliedThroughOffset`, applies each `queue-operation` record by the D5 lifecycle in the host binding table (every `enqueue` takes a queue position, system events as unminted `kind: system` entries; mint at a user `enqueue`, deliver at `dequeue` and `absorbed_mid_turn`, withdraw at other `remove` and `popAll`) to `turn-state.yaml` in one atomic replace that also advances `appliedThroughOffset`, skipping records that start below it, exits when `ended.yaml` with `reason: session_end` is written for its key (an idle end does not stop it; what-if X-6), a second start for the same key exits immediately, and a pid naming a dead or foreign process, or a bridge running another plugin cache version, is replaced by a bridge started from the active cache with `appliedThroughOffset` kept (architecture 4.4, RunArrivalBridge; `BridgeStalePidRestarts`, `BridgeRunningOtherCacheVersionRestartedFromActiveCacheOffsetKept`, `IdleEndedThenMidTurnMessageMintedAtEnqueue`); `Sync-PluginArrivalLog` (also called by the Stop hook and SessionStart, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003 AC-007) records the transcript length when a session-log verb starts and, after the verb takes `turn-open.lock`, applies only complete records that end at or before that length before the verb binds (records appended later are left for later invocations; `BindingDequeueAppendedAfterStartBeforeLockBindsToEarlier`), and on claude-code and claude-cowork the prompt hook neither mints nor claims. A4 extends AC-006 with the verb-side halves of the bridge cases, and A5 extends AC-005 with the rebind of real queued writes through the persist path. [A3 +A4 +A5]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002 Hook validator and installer (Claude plugin repo). AC-001 `Test-PluginEnabled` reads the `enabledPlugins` map and `known_marketplaces.json`; AC-002 `Get-DuplicateHookCommands` lists event:script duplicates; AC-003 validator JSON adds `duplicate`, `repaired`, `duplicateHooks`, `pluginEnabled`, `pluginKey`; AC-004 repair writes a backup and keeps non-MCP hooks; when the backup cannot be written, no settings file changes and the validator reports the failure (architecture 4.4, ValidateHookRegistration). [A2]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003 Per-turn store, pointer, target resolution, stop ledger (lib-ps). AC-001 `turns/<requestId>.yaml` plus `.lock`; the turn file holds the turn's `lastBuildStatus`, which code-verify (`Invoke-CodeVerify`, `plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1:1199` at `a8d3934b`, which today writes it into `current-turn.yaml` at `:1209,1262`) writes into the write target's file under that turn's lock, finding the host session from the hook payload's key as a verb does (a payload without the key writes nothing), and which the Stop gate's failed-build block reads (architecture 3.4 and 4.1; `CodeVerifyWritesLastBuildStatusToWriteTargetTurnFile`); AC-002 `Resolve-ReplTargetTurn` contract (process BindVerbToTurn, nested activity ResolveVerbTarget: precedence explicit requestId, else invocation binding; an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` while two or more delivered requests are open, D9; an unknown explicit id is refused with `request_unknown`; with one or no delivered request open the target is the write target even when it is closed, where every verb but `recordReview` and a requestClass-only update is refused with `turn_immutable`); AC-003 `Invoke-ReplSupersedeCurrentTurnIfInProgress` removed; AC-004 stop-ledger contract (`ledger` inside `turn-state.yaml`, written in the same atomic replace as the delivery it records); AC-005 per-turn edits never overwrite another turn's title (absorbs the intent of retired TR-MCP-REPL-019); AC-006 `Get-PluginHostSessionKey` implements the host binding table (invocation-context key, else, for verbs only, the live-session rule with `host_session_inferred`, `host_session_unknown`, `host_session_ambiguous`; a hook payload without the host row's key refuses and writes nothing), and `New-ReplInvocationBinding` captures `{ hostSessionKey, keySource, ingressNonce, requestId, boundAtUtc }` (C4; `ingressNonce` is the bound turn's nonce) once per verb invocation into its persist and failsafe records; AC-007 `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml` is written only by the arrival bridge, or a verb, the Stop hook, or SessionStart applying pending transcript records through `Sync-PluginArrivalLog` up to the transcript length at its own start (the Stop payload carries `transcript_path`; `StopGateBridgeDeadAppliesPendingRecordsBlocksDeliveredUnclosed`) (mint, delivery, withdrawal, `appliedThroughOffset`), the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge (mint and delivery), the close verbs (removing a request from the open delivered list only when the server confirms its close), the failsafe drain (replacing `pending-<nonce>` with the minted id in the write target and open list), the Stop gate (clearing ledger entries of confirmed-closed turns on a passing Stop, and recording `stop_gate_overridden_by_host` with the open turn ids when the host ends the session anyway), the first verb or hook in a host session that observes a failing copilot or classic-cline single-registration check (recording `unsupportedSince` with reason `duplicate_prompt_hook`), the first ingress event of a host session on a host without a SessionStart event (recording that host session's own `mcpSessionId` only when none is recorded, A8), and SessionStart (process StartHostSession, which a claude-code PostCompact run also runs, as does a prompt hook whose host session has no recorded `mcpSessionId`: recording a new `mcpSessionId` from `New-PluginSessionId` only when none is recorded for the key, after develop's trust bootstrap and header capture, and clearing `unsupportedSince` where its cause's own rule allows), each as one atomic replace under `turn-open.lock` through `Update-TurnState`, the one writer of the file (architecture 3.5.6); and `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/ended.yaml` (`{ reason: session_end | idle, endedAtUtc }` with the session-level envelope) only by the session-end hook (process EndHostSession, which also stops the bridge), the 12-hour idle rule, the revival of an idle-ended session by its next mint or keyed verb, and the revival of a `session_end`-ended key by a SessionStart for that key (each removal atomic under `turn-open.lock`; architecture 3.1, "Resumed host sessions"). From Phase C, `agentContextMode` and its two Mode cache writers (architecture 3.4) are specified in FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009's catalog. The arrival bridge, the mint, and every verb read the MCP session id only from their own host session's turn-state; the workspace-level `session-state.yaml` keeps develop's trust and header fields and is never read for targeting (architecture 3.1, "Host session start state"), and the rotated-sessionId rebind (`repl-invoke.ps1:1954-1965`, TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012) is removed (`TwoHostSessionsOwnMcpSessionIdsSecondSessionStartNeverRetargetsFirst`, `PostCompactSameHostSessionKeyKeepsMcpSessionIdOpenTurnClosesInOriginalSession`, `SessionEndMarkerResumeSessionStartRevivesKeepsMcpSessionId`). A5 extends AC-007 with the close verbs' server-confirmed removal, and A7 with the Stop gate's writes. [A4 +A5 +A7]

Rows.Domain: Turn arrival and binding
Rows.Text: - TEST-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 Ingress mint client, turn-open lock, and system-event classifier. Tests: `SessionTurnIntegrity.Tests.ps1` Describes `IngressMint`, `SystemEvents`, `TurnOpenLock`, `ArrivalBridge`; the refined prompt cases of `TriagePluginIdentity.Tests.ps1`, `SessionLogP2Contracts.Tests.ps1`, and `SessionLogLifecycle.Tests.ps1` (`#### Test churn`). Validates FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC001..AC004, -AC008 (including the mint-adapter 404, unknown-method, rollback, and negative cases of A3), -AC009, -AC010 (plugin side, including the arrival bridge and queue lifecycle), FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001, -AC002, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-001..AC-006. Also validates updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-001-AC007 (cases `SystemEventsHookReportsSkippedNoMint` and `ContendedTurnOpenLockReportsTurnOpenContendedNoMint`). Also validates the copilot equal-field rule of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC003 and TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-002 (cases `CopilotSamePromptDifferentTimestampTwoMints`, `CopilotEqualFieldsSecondInvocationFailsClosedNoSecondMint`, `CopilotMintRetryAndFailsafeReplayReuseNonceNoFailClose`). Also validates the bridge's unsupported-session transition of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009 (case `BridgeUnknownShapeOrTruncationAfterDeliveryRecordsUnsupportedSince`). Also validates `Sync-PluginArrivalLog` on its own (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-006, case `SyncArrivalLogAppliesOnlyRecordsUpToRecordedLength`). Its Cowork cases follow the P0.2 outcome: the two `BridgeCowork*` fixture cases when the Cowork probes pass, otherwise `CoworkP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites` (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC004); likewise, under the host binding table's P0.2 gating rule, each per-host mint case runs only when that host's P0.2 row passed, otherwise `ClaudeCodeP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `GrokP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `GrokBotP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, or `CopilotP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites` (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC004). Per the A3/A4 split, the A3 run of each bridge or fail-closed case asserts bridge and mint state only, and its verb-side half runs in A4 under the same case name. Also validates the system-event queue positions of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001 (cases `BridgeSystemEnqueueAheadOfUserSystemDequeueUserStaysQueued`, `BridgeSystemEnqueueRemovedNoTurn`, `BridgeSystemAndUserInterleavedCrashReplayZeroWrongTurnWrites`, `SystemEventsSubagentEnvMarkersNoMint`). Also validates the wrapper refusal of TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-004 (case `MintVerbWithoutHookInvocationRefusedMintRequiresHostIngress`, which it also contributes to TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-005, owner TEST-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004, the TEST that mirrors that TR) and the missing nonce source of TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-002 (case `NonceSourceMissingTurnOpenFailedFailsafeDiagnostic`). Also validates the REPL deprecation marker of TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-005 (case `MintTurnReplDeprecationMarkerIgnoredByCore`). Also validates the alias journal of TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-005 with synthetic queued records (cases `AliasJournalCrashBoundariesOneMintNoLostWrite`, `AliasJournalResolveEitherIdSameTurn`, `AliasJournalReplayNoReMint`; the real queued-write rebind is a TEST-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005 case), and the drain-time session open of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 (case `OutageSpanningSessionStartDrainOpensSessionThenMintsNotFinal`). Also validates updated TR-MCP-PLUGIN-013-AC001 (case `IngressMintRetryAndFailsafeReplayOneTurn`), TR-MCP-PLUGIN-013-AC002 (case `IngressMintIdenticalTextTwoEventsTwoTurns`), TR-MCP-PLUGIN-013-AC004 (case `SystemEventsHookReportsSkippedNoMint`), TEST-MCP-PLUGIN-013 AC001 under the P0.2 gating rule (cases `IngressMintTwoHookProcessesOneEventOneTurnPerMessageIdHosts`, `CopilotEqualFieldsSecondInvocationFailsClosedNoSecondMint`), and updated TEST-MCP-PLUGIN-011 AC001 (cases `PromptHookTaskNotificationNoPhantomTurn`, `SystemEventsHookReportsSkippedNoMint`). Changes: the store text's dedupe ("a repeated identical prompt reuses the already-open turn", and inline AC1 "the second delivery of the same prompt returns turn-already-open and does not call beginTurn"; implemented today as the prompt-text window at `plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1:796-835` at `a8d3934b`) is removed, and inline AC2 (a differing prompt opens a new turn) stays, restated by FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC004; each message event opens its turn through the server ingress mint with a nonce derived from that event (D1), so every delivery of one event gets one turn and identical prompts sent separately are separate turns, and a new prompt opens a new turn without canceling the open one. New ACs: TR-MCP-PLUGIN-013-AC001 a retried or replayed mint for one delivery opens one turn [A3]; -AC002 two separate deliveries of identical text open two turns [A3]; -AC003 a new prompt opens a new turn and leaves the prior turn in_progress [A4]; -AC004 system events open no turn [A3]. Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 Truthful persist outcomes.

Rows.Domain: Turn persistence, decision lists, and closing
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC001 Session submit returns a per-turn outcome, exactly one of `created`, `merged`, or `skipped_terminal`, with `storedStatus` and `reason` on REST, MCP `sessionlog_submit`, and the typed client; there is no `skipped_duplicate` outcome on any surface (operator, 2026-10-09: "Remove"); a resubmit identical to the stored turn reports `merged` with reason `no_change`; duplicate entries for one requestId in one submission are applied last-wins (today's behavior) and report one outcome for that requestId. The submit keeps status 201, and MCP `sessionlog_submit` returns `{ success, id, turns }` (architecture 4.2, SubmitSessionLogCommand). The outcome is decided by policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard (seam `ITerminalTurnOutcomeGuard`, architecture 4.3), which only the submit applies. The single-turn routes (turn upsert, PATCH, PUT, complete, fail) keep today's request and response bodies, report no per-turn outcome, and apply no terminal-turn outcome guard, because they are the explicit route for deliberate status corrections (`SessionLogService.cs:1610` at `a8d3934b`; `SingleTurnRoutesTerminalTurnStatusCorrectionTodayBodiesNoOutcomeGuard`, which extends the service-level `SessionLogSupersessionTests.UpsertTurnAsyncExplicitStatusCanCorrectTerminalTurn`, `SessionLogSupersessionTests.cs:125`, to every single-turn route). [A1]

Rows.Domain: Turn persistence, decision lists, and closing
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC002 The plugin maps `skipped_terminal` to `persisted:false`, code `skipped_terminal`, non-zero exit, and a cleared failsafe record. A retryable answer (a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, the answer a deadlock or busy store returns once SerializableWrite's four attempts are spent) keeps the write-ahead failsafe record and reports `persisted:false`, code `queued`, exit 0, and the request stays open and ledgered until the drain confirms the write; a final answer on a live verb clears the record and reports the server code with exit 1, except a `rejected` receipt (an outcome whose identity or readback is not confirmed), which keeps it; the failsafe drain stops at the first retryable answer without counting an attempt and keeps that record and every later one (FR-MCP-REPL-011). A review is the exception: it keeps its no-failsafe rule and reports the retryable code with exit 1 (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002, architecture 5.2). (Architecture 3.1, "Deadlock and busy outcomes" and "Retryable answers", and 4.4, PersistTurnWriteWithReceipt and SendBoundWrite; what-if W-2 and X-10, reconciled with the architecture: a retryable 409 is handled as an outage, never as a final refusal with exit 1 and no failsafe record.) [A5]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC006 Writes to different turns of one session never conflict: a single-turn write (turn upsert, PATCH, PUT, complete, fail) and the mint isolate the turn they write and its children, so two concurrent writes to different turns of one session both commit within the storage budget with no retryable answer, on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; a multi-turn submission keeps its session-level Serializable scope; the session summary refresh after a single-turn write is its own short write after the turn commits, and its failure never fails the turn write; a write whose transient conflict (deadlock, serialization failure, or busy store) outlasts SerializableWrite's four attempts, run within the unit's storage budget, answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing (operator, 2026-10-12, verbatim answer "Turn-level (Recommended)"; architecture 3.1 "Turn-level isolation", "Mint isolation", "Retry bound", and "Deadlock and busy outcomes", and 4.2, storage rules; recon `risk.md` R-R3). [A1]

Rows.Domain: Turn persistence, decision lists, and closing
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC007 Agent surfaces (REST, MCP, the typed client, the REPL, the plugin, and QBAgent's internal `mcp_session_turn_update` and `mcp_session_turn_complete` tools) write only the turn statuses `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, and the legacy `cancelled`; a submit, turn upsert, PATCH, or PUT naming `closed` or any other status is refused with 400 `validation_error`, `details.field` `status`, before any write, while server-internal writers and existing rows keep `closed` (operator, 2026-10-12, verbatim answer "Refuse from agent surfaces (Recommended)"; architecture 3.1, "Turn statuses on agent surfaces", 3.5.3, `TurnStatus`, and 4.2: the refusal lives in the handlers, and in `UpsertTurnAsync` for QBAgent's origin only). This AC is the one owner of the `closed` refusal; FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002, FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002, and FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001 cite it and add no AC of their own (coordinator ruling, 2026-10-13, `review-arch-r5/MERGE-BRIEF.md`; SessionTurnLogging owns `TurnStatus`, architecture 8.3). [A1]

Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005 The stop gate enforces and never closes turns.

Rows.Domain: Turn persistence, decision lists, and closing
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 Blocks with `turn_in_progress` when a delivered request in the stop ledger (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC004) is still in progress; a withdrawn request still in progress blocks under AC009, and a minted request still `queued` only warns. A request in state `queued` (minted, not yet delivered) never produces `turn_in_progress`; the gate warns, naming its requestId and enqueue time. A Stop in one host session never blocks or warns on another host session's turns (`StopGateOtherHostSessionNeverBlocksOrWarns`), and a Stop payload without the host row's session key is refused and writes nothing (architecture 4.4, EvaluateStopGate, and 3.1: "A write is never attributed by guesswork"; `StopGatePayloadWithoutHostSessionKeyRefusedWritesNothing`). A request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered, so a request minted before a passing Stop and delivered after it is evaluated at the next Stop (`StopGateEnqueueR2PassForR1DequeueR2NextStopBlocksUntilClosed`, including a restart between the two Stops). Unsupported-session failsafe: in a host session with `unsupportedSince` (whatever its reason, host binding table unsupported-session rule), every session-log write the model makes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) (evidence actions, design decisions, `requestClass`, and the close call; a review is never captured, keeping the no-failsafe rule of TR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005 AC-002 and S9, and is refused with `turn_logging_unsupported`) is captured as a plugin failsafe record that carries the turn's C4 binding and root-id envelope, is marked `unsupported_session`, and is never sent to the server during that host session; every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused with `turn_logging_unsupported` and captures nothing (`UnsupportedSessionMintOrWriteForOtherTurnRefusedNothingCaptured`). The Stop gate evaluates such a turn with its captured records counted: it blocks until the model's close is captured, with a remedy that names only the missing model evidence, the missing `requestClass` (from S8/S9, when the plugin's requestClass verb ships; a class write is captured like any other write), and the close call (all accepted, AC002; the plugin pre-check lets that close through, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004-AC002), because only the completion gate's terminal reviews cannot be written in that session; it then only warns with the cause and the retained failsafe records. The completion gate is judged at the drain: the server's gate judges the drained close, and a gate rejection keeps the turn in progress and listed with its original pair at that SessionStart, where its reviews are recorded through the C5 pair (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002-AC002) before it is closed (`UnsupportedSessionReviewRefusedNotCaptured`, `UnsupportedSessionCodeTurnDrainedCloseRejectedByGateStaysListedReviewViaPairThenCloses`). The first SessionStart for the agent after that host session has ended, or a SessionStart that clears its cause under its rule, drains the captured records in original order through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair (C5); a post-compact or other SessionStart of the still-live host session drains none of them and counts no attempt (FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002; `DrainUnsupportedSessionRecordOfLiveHostSessionNotDrainedNoAttemptCounted`), and a record whose turn is no longer in progress on the server moves to the failsafe quarantine with its `.reason.txt` and is never forced onto that turn (architecture 4.4, DrainFailsafe and ReplayBoundRecord; what-if X-4 settled there; `DrainUnsupportedSessionRecordTurnNoLongerInProgressQuarantinedNeverForced`). Each reason is covered from an earlier open turn (`StopGateUnknownBridgeRecordEarlierOpenTurnCloseCapturedThenWarnsOnly`, `StopGateTruncatedTranscriptEarlierOpenTurnCloseCapturedThenWarnsOnly`, `StopGateSyntheticUnsupportedSinceAnyReasonEarlierOpenTurnCloseCapturedThenWarnsOnly` in A7; the real duplicate-hook transition `DuplicateHookAfterDeliveryUnsupportedSinceOpenTurnCloseCaptured` for copilot in A9 and `ClineDuplicateHookAfterDeliveryUnsupportedSinceOpenTurnCloseCaptured` for classic cline in A8). A withdrawn-before-delivery turn is covered too: its decision, its `requestClass` (from S8/S9), and `failTurn` by original pair are captured, the next Stop warns instead of blocking, and the drain closes it (after S10 the server gate accepts that fail, which needs only the class) (`StopGateWithdrawnBeforeDeliveryThenUnsupportedCloseCapturedByPairNextStopWarnsDrainCloses`). A Stop in another live host session still blocks on that session's own turns (`StopGateEqualFieldFailClosedEarlierOpenTurnCloseCapturedToFailsafeThenWarnsOnlyDrainsWithOriginalPair`, `StopGateBridgeAmbiguityEarlierOpenTurnCloseCapturedToFailsafeThenWarnsOnlyDrainsWithOriginalPair`). Outage close: a model close, a withdrawn request's `failTurn` (AC009), or, from Phase C, the plugin's package-failure `canceled` close (process RunStatelessInvocation; it never needs model evidence) held in the ordinary plugin failsafe by a retryable answer (a transport outage, a retryable 503, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, architecture 3.1, "Retryable answers") turns that turn's block into the existing degraded persistence warning (AC005, naming the package failure for the `canceled` close); its ledger entry stays until the server confirms the close (`StopGateOutageCloseQueuedWarnsDegradedLedgerKeptUntilConfirmed`; `StatelessPackageFailureCancelCloseQueuedByOutageStopWarnsDegradedDrainConfirmsAndClears` in AgentContextPluginCore, what-if WC-M1). [A7 +A8 +A9 +S8 +S10 +AgentContextPluginCore]

Rows.Domain: Turn persistence, decision lists, and closing
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002 The plugin close verbs refuse to close a turn that has no model-authored action, design decision, or commit (`Test-ModelEvidence`, architecture 3.5.6, which counts the turn's records captured in the failsafe and never a hook invocation; the evidence predicate TR-MCP-PLUGIN-011-AC003 keeps), with code `turn_missing_model_evidence`; the turn stays in progress, so the stop gate blocks it as `turn_in_progress` with the accumulated remedy of the wire contract (every unmet prerequisite, then the valid close call, computed by `Get-CloseRemedy`, architecture 3.5.6). A turn closed without model evidence by another surface accepts no plugin edit, so the gate reports it as a warning naming it and never blocks on it. Every stop-gate block names a remedy the plugin accepts on the blocked turn's current status (`StopGateEveryBlockRemedyAcceptedOnBlockedTurnStatus`, `CloseVerbNoEvidenceRefusedTurnStaysInProgress`, `StopGateClosedWithoutEvidenceElsewhereWarnsOnly`, `CloseVerbCommitOnlyEvidenceAccepted`). [A7 +A8]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC003 Blocks with `session_turn_completion_gate` a turn whose most recent close the server refused with that code (recorded locally from the server response; such a turn is still in progress), naming the server's missing items first in its remedy (`StopGateServerGateRefusalBlocksWithServerMissingItems`), except for an already open turn of a host session with `unsupportedSince`, whose completion gate is judged at the drain (AC001); that exception is evaluated before a remembered refusal can block (`StopGateGateRefusedThenUnsupportedSinceCloseCapturedWarnsNotBlocks`). There is no marker condition: the server gate (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002) is the only completion authority. Its remedy is the accumulated per-turn remedy of the wire contract, so it also names any missing model evidence. [S8 +S9 +S10]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC005 Warns without blocking for model-canceled turns, retained failsafe records, and degraded persistence. The warning list is exactly the architecture's (4.4, EvaluateStopGate, Warnings). Per turn: model-canceled turns (a plugin `canceled` close names its package failure), a turn closed without model evidence by another surface, degraded persistence (a model close, a withdrawn request's `failTurn`, or the plugin's package-failure `canceled` close held in the failsafe by a retryable answer, AC001), a captured unsupported-session close (naming the `unsupportedSince` reason and the captured records), and queued undelivered requests (naming the requestId and enqueue time). Per host session: each `unsupportedSince` reason (`queue_removal_ambiguous`, `indistinguishable_arrival`, `duplicate_prompt_hook`, `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, or any other) naming the open turns of its fail-closed host session and their captured `unsupported_session` failsafe records; retained failsafe records, which are a mint refused for a final reason, queued or quarantined, and an `open-failed` queue entry, each naming the prompt, and every quarantined record of an open turn with its reason (what-if W-8; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 and -AC010); `duplicate_delivery_suspected`; `nonce_source_missing` and `turn-open-contended`, each naming the prompt (what-if W-5); `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`; an earlier `stop_gate_overridden_by_host`; a live bridge host session whose arrival bridge is not running; and a turn in progress in the legacy `current-turn.yaml` at upgrade (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC004, `StopGateLegacyCurrentTurnInProgressWarned`). Open turns of ended host sessions are not a Stop warning, because a Stop never blocks or warns on another host session's turns (AC001); the next SessionStart lists them with their pairs (AC006; what-if X-9). A legacy failsafe record that names no request is quarantined by the drain and belongs to no open turn, so it is no Stop warning; plugin Status counts it with the quarantine counts (architecture 3.1, "Quarantined legacy records"; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC004; `plugins/core/lib-ps/mcp-status.ps1:85-88` at `a8d3934b`). [A7 +AgentContextPluginCore]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC006 Passes and clears the ledger only when every check passes. Every Stop invocation re-evaluates the ledger, including when the host reports that an earlier Stop already blocked (Claude Code `stop_hook_active`, Grok `stopHookActive`): while any turn remains open it blocks again with the same findings. If the host ends the session anyway (its own continuation limit), the gate records `stop_gate_overridden_by_host` with the open turn ids in the ledger, and the next SessionStart or prompt hook shows it as a warning until the model closes those turns. A ledger entry whose closing write the server has not confirmed terminal stays in the ledger across passing Stops until the server reports it terminal. Turns still in progress when their host session ends (any reason, including `/clear` and a host override) stay in progress and are listed at the next SessionStart for that agent in the workspace with their original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pairs; closing one through the trusted recovery flow with that pair succeeds, and a `requestId` alone is refused (C5). [A7 +A8]

Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 Server per-turn submit outcomes, ingress mint, and turn write isolation (architecture 4.1 to 4.3; each command record and its handler are two files under `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/`, namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.SessionLog.Commands`). AC-001 SubmitSessionLogCommand delegates to `ISessionLogService.SubmitWithOutcomesAsync`, which upserts the session row and runs TurnWritePipeline in mode `Submit` for each turn inside one session-level SerializableWrite; `SubmitAsync` delegates to it; every unit of this TR also answers WorkspaceResolutionBehavior's 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `workspacePath` after its dispatch (architecture 3.5.1 and 4.2; tested once by that behavior's cases in SharedComponents), which the plugin reports as a final code; AC-002 the seam `ITerminalTurnOutcomeGuard` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.SessionLog`, policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard, architecture 4.3) replaces the inline guard at `SessionLogService.cs:1606-1618` (at `a8d3934b`) without changing its rule, and only mode `Submit` applies it; AC-003 `SessionLogSubmitResult.turns` on REST (status 201), MCP `sessionlog_submit` (`{ success, id, turns }`), the client, and the REPL strategy; AC-004 the decorators `SessionLogSanitizingService`, `FederatedSessionLogService`, and `TransactionGatedSessionLogService` forward `SubmitWithOutcomesAsync` and `MintTurnAsync`; AC-005 a new mint operation (MintSessionTurnCommand; its DTOs `SessionLogMintTurnRequest` and `SessionLogMintTurnResult` in `src/QBrainAi.Client/Models/SessionLog/`, namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Models.SessionLog`), because the existing begin route requires `{requestId}` in its path (`SessionLogController.cs:388-396`) and the client interpolates it (`SessionLogClient.cs:174-191`): REST `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint` (the controller's second route attribute also serves it under `/mcpserver/sessionlog`, `SessionLogController.cs:15-16`) with body `SessionLogMintTurnRequest { ingressNonce (required, `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$`), queryTitle, queryText, model, planFile (required; path or `None`), todoId (required; TODO id or `None`) }` validated like the begin body (`docs/context/session-log-schema.md:16,64-66`); responses 201 `{ requestId, outcome: "created" }`, 200 `{ requestId, outcome: "merged", storedStatus }` when the nonce already exists in that session, 400 `ingress_nonce_invalid`, 400 `validation_error` for an invalid session id (TurnLocator `InvalidIdentifier`) or the existing planFile/todoId validation errors, 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` after SerializableWrite's four attempts (nothing saved; the plugin keeps its failsafe mint record as for an outage), 404 with detail code `session_not_open` when the session is not open (only the trusted mint adapter interprets an authenticated, bound mint-endpoint 404 without a detail code as a missing route, as on a server older than A1, per FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 and the scoped C9 exception); no MCP tool (the mint is not a model-visible tool; every `[McpServerTool]` in `FwhMcpTools.SessionLog.cs` is model-visible); client `MintTurnAsync(agent, sessionId, ingressNonce, queryTitle, queryText, model, planFile, todoId)`; REPL `workflow.sessionlog.mintTurn`, which the plugin wrappers refuse with `mint_requires_host_ingress` unless the call comes from a hook or adapter entry point (`MCP_PLUGIN_HOOK_INVOCATION=1`; a guard against accidental model use, not a security boundary) and which no model-facing skill or tool description mentions; the begin route and `BeginTurnAsync` keep today's behavior; AC-006 `SessionLogTurnEntity.IngressNonce` (string 64, nullable) with a unique filtered index on (WorkspaceId, SessionLogId, IngressNonce) where not null and a second unique filtered index on (WorkspaceId, RequestId) where IngressNonce is not null (minted ids are workspace-unique across sessions; legacy rows are untouched), added by migration `<utc>_AddSessionLogTurnIngressNonce` for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server (StorageSchema); the mint is IdempotentCreate keyed by (session, ingressNonce) with policy `ReturnStored` inside SerializableWrite, and a single-turn write under turn-level isolation (architecture 3.1, "Mint isolation", and 3.5.2): a mint whose nonce exists returns the stored turn's requestId as `merged` whatever the payload; a violation of the nonce index ends the attempt, and SerializableWrite's rerun returns the winner as `merged`; the insert takes its requestId from ReadableKeyAllocator strategy `RandomHex` (InsertMintedTurnWithRetry, architecture 4.2; the `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>` format is tested once, as `ReadableKeyAllocatorTests.ReadableKeyAllocatorRandomHexRequestIdFormatCollisionNextCandidate` of TR-MCP-SHAREDPLATFORM-001, SharedComponents), and a violation of the requestId index is a declared key collision retried with the next candidate up to 6 attempts in all, then 500 `mint_collision_exhausted` (C9 ACKed by Codex at 2026-10-09T23:22:30Z); a transient conflict keeps SerializableWrite's default bound (four attempts), then 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and nothing saved; any other database error fails the mint; AC-007 every turn write runs TurnWritePipeline inside SerializableWrite (architecture 3.5.2, 3.5.3, and 4.2, storage rules), using the components as TR-MCP-SHAREDPLATFORM-001 AC-001 (`DbErrorClassifier`) and AC-002 (`SerializableWrite`, with its bound, its in-memory single run, and its caller-owned transaction refusal) define them, which this AC does not restate; it states their use by the turn writes: a single-turn write (upsert, patch, replace, complete, fail) and the mint read and write only their session row and their turn with its children (turn-level isolation), a submission keeps its session-level scope, and the session summary refresh after a single-turn write is its own short write after the turn commits, whose failure never fails the turn write; the turn writes call `DbErrorClassifier` in place of develop's message-text predicates (`SessionLogService.cs:234,357,764-797,812-817` at `a8d3934b`); their four attempts run within the unit's storage budget, then 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and nothing saved; and develop's own turn-write cases for the caller-owned transaction refusal (`SessionLogService.cs:119-128`) and the single in-memory run (`SessionLogService.cs:155`) keep their outcome (section "Test churn"). [A1]

Changes: title becomes "Session-log persist outcomes"; AC001 enumerates four outcomes (primary persisted, degraded queued, failed/lost, and per-turn skipped_terminal); AC002 adds per-turn `turns[]` outcome fields; AC003 "honored only when it matches the active turn" becomes "honored when it identifies the current or a registered open turn"; statement "appendActions refuses a request-id mismatch" becomes "refuses an unknown requestId"; AC006 ("Write-ahead recovery is retained before backend submission and deleted only after durable confirmation") keeps its text, and its outcome now also holds for 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (architecture 3.1, "Deadlock and busy outcomes", which names this ac6; its cases are FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC002's); AC007's "or returns one classified retryable outcome inside that budget" names that outcome: 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` once SerializableWrite's four attempts are spent inside the submit's storage budget, with no partial or duplicate child row (architecture 3.5.2) [A1]. New ACs: FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-005-AC006 the stop gate never closes a turn [A7]; -AC007 it blocks while a delivered request (the stop ledger, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC004) is in_progress, blocks a withdrawn request still in_progress with `turn_withdrawn_unclosed`, and only warns for a minted request still `queued` although its server turn is in_progress (D5) [A7].
