Changes: the statement's "automatically on the first proven-reachable call and on demand through an explicit drain verb" becomes "automatically at each per-host-session trigger (SessionStart, and the next prompt hook or verb whose host session's failsafe holds drainable records) and on demand through the explicit drain verb, which follows the same rules", and "a record the backend rejects does not block the newer records behind it" becomes "a record the backend refuses with a final answer counts one drain attempt and holds back only the later records of its own turn"; AC001's "both automatic proven-reachable replay and explicit drain" becomes "every drain trigger" (the first-success trigger `Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccess`, `repl-invoke.ps1:1188-1238` at `a8d3934b`, wired in `Invoke-ReplRaw` at `:652-655`, is removed; architecture: "this replaces the first-success trigger of FR-MCP-REPL-011 ac1") [A5]; AC002 "deleted only after the backend confirms durable persistence" becomes "deleted only after a confirmed answer for its exact workspace, agent, session, and request: a `persisted` receipt (with `outcomeVerified: false` included), `unchanged`, `skipped_terminal`, or a mint that returns a turn" [A5]; AC003 becomes "A final answer increments the record's `drainAttempts` and the walk continues, skipping only the later records bound to the same turn while that turn's mint or write is unresolved; a malformed record, a record at the attempt budget of 5 (0 again after a repair), a legacy record that names no request, a write bound to a pending id whose mint is quarantined, and an `unsupported_session` record whose turn is no longer in progress move to the quarantine subdirectory with a `.reason.txt`, are never deleted, and never replay from there" [A5]; AC005's second sentence becomes "A timeout abort leaves `drainAttempts` unchanged; no REPL call starts a nested drain, and there is no completion latch" [A5]. New ACs: FR-MCP-REPL-011-AC006 a retryable answer (a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`) stops the walk without counting an attempt and keeps that record and every later one [A5]; -AC007 a record with a captured binding replays through it (the idempotent session open for its envelope `mcpSessionId` first, then the mint or the write under the journaled alias, the bound id, or the original pair), a legacy record whose parameters name its session and request replays its method and parameters as today, and an `unsupported_session` record of a host session still live with `unsupportedSince` is not drained and counts no attempt [A5].

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001 (FR:1268) "Shared clear-session reset skill for all agent plugins". The store holds no AC for it (`acceptanceCriteria: []`), so the earlier "inline AC1" named a clause that exists only in TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001 (recon `req-ab.md`). Changes: the statement's step "(1) end the current MCP session" becomes "(1) finalize each open request turn of the host session by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair per the clear-session closing rule, then end the current MCP session", and "All QBrain.AI agent plugins" is the nine plugins (grok-bot added, D8). New ACs: FR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001 before it ends the MCP session, clear-session finalizes each open request turn of the host session (a delivered request still open, a withdrawn entry still in progress, and a minted request still `queued`) by its original pair: failed when withdrawn or still queued (reason "withdrawn before delivery") or marked blocked (its first blocker as the reason), completed when it meets the completion policy and has model evidence, otherwise left in progress and reported with its exact missing items; a turn the server already reports terminal is reported closed elsewhere with its `storedStatus` and nothing is sent; no review is ever fabricated (architecture 3.1, clear-session closing rule, and 5.4, ClearSession) [S8 +S9 +S10]; -AC002 every one of the nine plugins provides the same clear-session skill [S9].

Rows.Domain: Turn persistence, decision lists, and closing
Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001 (TR:661) "clear-session skill content contract". Changes: inline AC1 "end the session by finalizing the open turn via workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn" becomes "end the session by finalizing each open request turn per TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001 (completeTurn, failTurn, or left in progress)" [S8 coordinator +S9 skill text], and "byte-identical in all 8 agent plugin repositories" becomes all nine [S9]. Phasing: S8 ships the PowerShell clear-session coordinator runtime in the synced plugin core with its PowerShell RED cases and edits no skill text; because `SyncAgentPlugins` does not copy this skill, S9, once the TypeScript hosts reach the S8 coordinator through their adapters, edits the clear-session skill text in all nine plugin repos at once (the six PowerShell hosts and cline, cline-v2, opencode). Its evidence is application evidence, so it runs in application suites, never in Build.Tests, which is infrastructure and evidences only TR-MCP-NUKE TRs (architecture 3.1, "Test placement"): each repo's `tests/Skills.Tests.ps1` case `ClearSessionSkillListsSelectionAndGateSteps` (extending today's clear-session case, `mcpserver-claude-code-plugin/tests/Skills.Tests.ps1:29-33` at the repo's current head) runs in G6 through `./build.ps1 TestAgentPlugins`, and the PluginIntegration case `ClearSessionSkillNineReposByteIdenticalListsSelectionAndGateSteps` reads `skills/clear-session/SKILL.md` from the nine repos of the scenario catalog under the sibling plugin parent (`PluginSessionLogCatalog.SiblingPluginParent`, `tests/QBrainAi.PluginIntegration.Tests/PluginSessionLogCatalog.cs:36-57` at `a8d3934b`, which resolves `/home/sharpninja/github` from a worktree) and runs in G3 through `./build.ps1 PluginSessionLogIntegration`; it fails, never skips, when fewer than nine repos are found. This replaces the earlier Build.Tests hosting of `ClearSessionSkillNineReposByteIdenticalListsSelectionSteps` and `ClearSessionSkillListsGateSteps`, its direct test-runner step outside Nuke, and its `MCP_AGENT_PLUGIN_PARENT` hand-off to `ResolveAgentPluginParentDirectory`. New ACs: TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001 clear-session selects with the shared completion policy before any close, so it holds before S10, for each open request turn addressed by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair: a delivered request still open, a `withdrawn` entry still in progress, and a minted request still `queued` (architecture 5.4, ClearSession; what-if Q-9). A turn the server already reports terminal from any surface is reported closed elsewhere with its `storedStatus`, and nothing is sent. Otherwise, in this precedence: a withdrawn turn, or a minted request still `queued`, is failed (reason "withdrawn before delivery"); else a turn marked blocked is failed with its blocker reason (blocked takes precedence over a ready completion); else a turn whose completion gate and model-evidence check (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002) are met is completed; else it stays in progress, reported by requestId with its exact missing items; `failed` requires `requestClass` only, and no review is ever fabricated. "Marked blocked" means the turn's `blockers` section (the existing decision-list field, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001) holds at least one nonblank model-authored entry, read by the coordinator for that turn by its original pair; the first entry is the fail reason (operator option A, 2026-10-10). Before failing a withdrawn or blocked turn, the coordinator checks its close prerequisites in the Stop gate remedy order (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009): model evidence (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002) and a `requestClass` that is neither missing nor `Unclassified`. A turn that lacks one is not sent to `failTurn`: the coordinator reports it by requestId with its `queryText`, the reason it will be failed with, and each missing prerequisite; within the same clear-session run, before its session-end step, the model writes them by the original pair (a designDecision, then the class, Code, Docs, or Chore, judged from that `queryText`), and the coordinator runs again, reads them back by that pair, and fails the turn with its reason, so neither the plugin's evidence check nor the server gate refuses a clear-session fail. In a host session with `unsupportedSince`, `Get-CloseRemedy` counts the turn's captured `unsupported_session` records as written, as the Stop gate does, and a captured close is reported as captured for the next SessionStart drain (what-if W-16). Each close goes through processes BindVerbToTurn and PersistTurnWriteWithReceipt by the original pair, and its receipt is reported (nested activity ReportCloseReceipt): `persisted` as closed, `skipped_terminal` as closed elsewhere with its `storedStatus`, `outcomeVerified: false` as unverified and not counted closed (the coordinator is rerun), a retryable answer (a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`) as queued in the failsafe and drained later, a captured close as captured, and a refusal or another server code as left in progress with that code (and, for `session_turn_completion_gate`, the server's missing items) [S8 +S9 +S10]; TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC002 the clear-session skill text is byte-identical in all nine plugin repos, PowerShell only, and lists the selection and gate steps, evidenced by TEST-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001 through `ClearSessionSkillListsSelectionAndGateSteps` (G6) and `ClearSessionSkillNineReposByteIdenticalListsSelectionAndGateSteps` (G3) [S9; S11 re-runs it].

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001-AC002 Other values, empty strings, and `Unclassified` from agent surfaces are rejected with 400 `request_class_invalid` (policy RequestClassification, architecture 5.3), and nothing of that write is saved. [S1 +S5]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001-AC003 An omitted value keeps the stored value on additive writes; PUT replace resets it. [S4]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001-AC004 The migration backfills every existing row with `Unclassified`, soft-deleted rows included, so a soft-deleted row reads `Unclassified` after it is revived (`BackfillSoftDeletedRowsUnclassifiedAndUnstartedAfterRevive`). The column's database default is `Unclassified`, so a turn the prior binary inserts during a binary-only rollback reads `Unclassified` after the roll-forward, which runs no second backfill (`RollbackPriorBinaryInsertsTurnRollForwardReadsDefaults`, architecture 5.1 and 8.5); a turn the new binary inserts keeps a null class until it is classified. [S3]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001-AC005 Turns can be created and updated without a class. [S4]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001-AC006 The field is readable and writable on REST, MCP, client, REPL, and McpAgent, and writable through QBAgent's `mcp_session_turn_complete` (TR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004 AC-004). Every read surface returns it through `TurnReadProjection` (architecture 3.5.3). MCP `sessionlog_complete_turn` and `sessionlog_fail_turn` copy `requestClass` from `turnJson` in addition to the fields `FinalizeLifecycleTurnToolAsync` copies today, and copy no review (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.SessionLog.cs:328-369` at `a8d3934b`; architecture 4.5, CompleteSessionTurnCommand sequence). [S5 +S6 +S7]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002 Completion gate.

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC001 `completed` requires `requestClass`, `agentReview` in Pass/Fail/Other, and for Code/Docs `hostileReview` in Pass/Fail/Other; for Chore `hostileReview` is not checked. For the gate `Unclassified` counts as missing, and a missing class is not `Chore`, so a `completed` write with no class also lists `hostileReview` and following the missing items literally passes whichever class the model then sets (policy CompletionPolicy, architecture 5.3; `CompletionPolicyMissingClassRequiresHostileReviewAsNonChore`). The gate evaluates the turn as it will be stored after the same write's review records (policy ReviewValidation), class change, and Chore flip (policy RequestClassification), in that order inside `TurnWritePipeline` (architecture 3.5.3), so one write carrying `requestClass`, terminal reviews, and `completed` succeeds. [S1 policy, S10 enforcement]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC002 `failed` requires `requestClass` only. [S1, S10]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC003 The gate applies on every surface: submit, upsert, PATCH, PUT, complete, fail, MCP tools, REPL, McpAgent, and QBAgent's internal session-turn tools (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-003-AC004); the plugin, REPL-workflow, and McpAgent verbs close through submit (SubmitSessionLogCommand, architecture 4.2). [S10]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC004 It fires only on a write that moves the turn into `completed` or `failed`, or on a PUT whose replacement carries `completed` or `failed` even when the stored status already equals it (a whole replacement is not enrichment, architecture 4.2). A write that only enriches an already terminal turn is not re-gated, including a requestClass-only change that leaves a terminal turn failing the completion policy (for example `Chore` to `Code` with hostile `Unnecessary`), which is accepted and changes no review (`ClassOnlyChangeOnCompletedTurnLeavesPolicyUnmetAcceptedNotRegated`; architecture 3.1, round-5 resolutions). A transition into `canceled` or the legacy `cancelled` is not a completion and is not gated, a deliberate difference from the QBAgent evidence gate (`TurnStatus.IsTerminal`, develop's `IsTerminalTurnStatus`, counts both), so that client-supplied canceled persists (FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001) and the plugin's own `canceled` close of a failed Phase C invocation (architecture 6.6) keep working; it never satisfies the gate, and the Stop gate warns a canceled turn as model-canceled. A status outside the agent write set (`closed` included) is refused with 400 `validation_error`, `details.field` `status`, before the gate, by the agent status rule that FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC007 owns (turn-persistence domain; `TurnStatus`, architecture 3.5.3), so `closed` never bypasses the gate (UC-5 alternate flow E5). [S10]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC005 A rejection is atomic and leaves the data context reusable: the gate check and the save run as one `SerializableWrite` delegate, which rolls the rejected write back, so nothing of it is saved (architecture 3.4, Write isolation, and 3.5.2). A submission in which any turn fails the gate is rejected as a whole, after every turn is evaluated, with 400 `session_turn_completion_gate` naming each failing requestId with its missing items, and no turn of that submission is persisted. A concurrent review reset, class change (a Chore flip included), review write, or close of the same turn commits wholly before or after the gated write, never between its gate check and its save (`TurnWriteForcedInterleavingReviewResetVsCompleteNeverClosedWithoutReview`, `TurnWriteForcedInterleavingClassChangeVsCompleteGateSeesCommittedClass`, each on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server at the gate of the CompletionGate enforcement change set, architecture 8.4). When `SerializableWrite`'s default bound (four attempts) is exhausted, the gated write answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing (`GatedCloseWriteBoundExhausted409ConflictRetryableNothingSaved`, the unit mapping the component's exhaustion exit through its Phase 2 seam; the component's own case belongs to SharedComponents). [S10]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC006 The error is 400 `validation_error` with `retryable: false`, its message starting with the token `session_turn_completion_gate` and listing the missing items in fixed order (requestClass, agentReview, hostileReview). The handler fails with `ClassifiedErrorException` (architecture 3.5.2); REST returns the `ClassifiedError` problem+json body and MCP the classified error object through the one `ClassifiedErrorException` branch of `McpErrorClassifier`, with no gate-specific branch (`CompletionGateRefusalBodyTokenAndMissingItemsInOrderRestAndMcp`). [S1 message, S5 surface mapping, S10]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-003-AC001 Import (`SessionLogIngestor`, `TranscriptSessionLogPersister`), ServerInternal (`AuditedAgentCliClient`, `WorkspacePolicyService`, `QuadBrainOpenAiChatService`), and Replication (federation apply) origins bypass the gate (policy CompletionGate, architecture 5.3). Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-003-AC002 ServerInternal writers stamp `Chore`; Import and Replication stamp `Unclassified` when no class arrives; no review is ever fabricated. Import and Replication store a supplied review record exactly as received (status and stamped thresholds, not re-derived) after the same per-status and score validation as Agent writes (policy ReviewValidation, architecture 5.3); an invalid record is rejected with its `review_*` code. [S10]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-003-AC003 No REST, MCP, REPL, client, or plugin code can select a non-Agent origin (architecture test). [S10]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-003-AC004 QBAgent's internal session-turn tools are gated Agent-origin writers: `mcp_session_turn_update` and `mcp_session_turn_complete` call `ISessionLogService.UpsertTurnAsync` directly (`QuadBrainInternalToolExecutor.cs:299-328` at `a8d3934b`), which applies the agent status rule (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC007, whose owning TEST holds the QBAgent `closed` case `QBAgentTurnUpdateToolClosedStatusRefused400`) and the gate to them. A `mcp_session_turn_complete` call without a class or terminal reviews fails with the gate's refusal and stores nothing, and one that carries its optional `requestClass`, `agentReview`, and `hostileReview` arguments (TR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004 AC-004) completes (`QbAgentTurnCompleteToolWithoutClassOrReviewsRefusedWithThemCompletes`; architecture 3.1, "Completion gate writers"). Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004-AC002 The local pre-check is advisory: before the close is sent it computes the missing completion items with the exact gate message (the golden-contract rules) and reports them as a warning; it never refuses a close. A class or review recorded by another process, host session, or surface before the completion is honored and is not reported missing. The server gate (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002, S10) is the only completion authority, so nothing refuses a close that a pre-S10 or rolled-back server would accept, and no activation signal is needed: the gate adds no marker field, and nothing of FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004 changes the marker or its signature (the contract digest and signature values change only through FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC005's nine `agent_plugins` contracts, with the signed field list of TR-MCP-SEC-005 unchanged, in the plugin-hosts domain). When the server refuses a close with 400 `session_turn_completion_gate`, the surface reports the server's message and missing items, the turn stays in progress, and AC003 applies (`PrecheckAdvisoryWarnsMissingItemsNeverRefuses`). Unsupported session (operator option 1, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001): for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning), the close goes to the `unsupported_session` failsafe with no server write per FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 (the advisory warning still prints), and the server gate judges it at the drain after its host session ends or its cause is cleared (architecture 4.5, close sequence); the model-evidence check (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002) still applies. This is plugin-core state only; the McpAgent pre-check of TR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004 has no host session (`PrecheckUnsupportedSessionCodeTurnMissingReviewsCloseCapturedNoServerWrite`). [S8 +S10]

Rows.Domain: Request class and the completion gate
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004-AC003 A close that carries actions, decisions, requirements, or blockers is sent as two writes: the carried evidence first, as an additive write that changes no status (so the completion gate never applies to it, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC004) and is verified by readback against the sanitized read projection (GetSessionLogQuery through `TurnReadProjection`, architecture 3.1 and 5.2), then the status transition. If the evidence write is refused with a final code (a server refusal, or `transaction_degraded` or `mutation_not_transactional` from the REPL's client mutation policy), the transition is not sent, the turn stays in progress, and the receipt carries that code with `persisted: false`, exit 1 (`CloseWithEvidenceEvidenceWriteRefusedFinalCodeTransitionNotSentTurnStaysOpen` against a server double in S8, named in the owner TEST-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005). If it is answered with a retryable answer (a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`), the failsafe keeps two records in order, the evidence write and then the close, the receipt is `queued` with exit 0, and the Stop ledger keeps the request until the drain confirms the close (architecture 4.5, close sequence). The failsafe keeps each part until that part is verified on the server, so a crash between them replays only what is missing and replay is idempotent. A server gate rejection of the transition therefore loses no evidence: it clears only the transition part, leaves the turn in progress, and reports the refusal with the server's missing items (`CloseWithEvidenceEvidenceWriteVerifiedBeforeTransitionGateRefusalLosesNothing` against a server double in S8; `RealGateRejectedCloseEvidenceSurvivesRestartReadBackEveryField` against the real gate in S10). This includes a drained `unsupported_session` close: its `session_turn_completion_gate` rejection clears that failsafe record and keeps the turn in progress and listed with its original pair. The close's carried writes follow this rule until its reviews are recorded through the C5 pair and a later close is accepted (`UnsupportedSessionCodeTurnDrainedCloseRejectedByGateStaysListedReviewViaPairThenCloses`, run against the real gate in S10). [S8 +S10]

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001-AC003 A review write replaces the whole record (latest wins, reasons not merged); an identical write is a no-op. A no-op is a write whose resulting stored record (derived status and stamps included) equals the current one. [S4]

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001-AC004 An omitted review keeps the stored record (the `Merge` modes); a PUT turn omitting it and a review section DELETE (REST, client `ClearTurnReviewAsync`, and MCP `sessionlog_clear_section` with a review section or alias, each dispatching ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand) reset it to the default status. The default status is the creation default for the turn's current class (`ReviewDefaults`): `hostileReview` `Unnecessary` when the class is Chore, otherwise `Unstarted`; `agentReview` `Unstarted`. On a `completed` or `failed` turn a review section DELETE is refused with 400 `review_section_reset_on_terminal_turn` and changes nothing; a turn that is `in_progress`, `canceled`, `cancelled`, or `closed` is reset (architecture 5.2, ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand). [S4 +S5]

A review keeps its no-failsafe rule (an older review must never overwrite a newer one), so the plugin `recordReview` verb reports that answer, a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, and a busy store's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true` each with `persisted: false`, the answer's code, and `retryable: true`, exit 1, never `queued`, and the model records the review again for the same turn after the drain (architecture 3.1 "Retryable answers", 5.2 RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand, UC-6). Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-003-AC006 Scores lie in [0,1]; `reviewer` <= 256 chars; paths <= 2048 chars; `reviewedAt` needs an explicit offset and is stored UTC; reason items are non-empty. Each violation returns exactly one code from the wire-contract error list, identical on REST, MCP, client, REPL (the REPL classifier carries the server's `ClassifiedError` through at every status, architecture 3.5.2), and the PowerShell plugin core (golden contract). The field-to-code map is: `reviewer` over 256 characters or a receipt path over 2048 characters gives `review_field_too_long` naming the field and limit; `reviewedAt` without an explicit offset or not a valid ISO-8601 instant gives `review_timestamp_invalid`; an empty or whitespace-only reason item gives `review_reason_blank`; each is asserted with the same code and HTTP 400 by the golden contract in C# and Pester (`GoldenContractFieldToCodeMapAllSurfaces`: C# in S1, REST/MCP/client in S5, REPL in S6, Pester in S8). When one write has several violations, every surface returns the first in one order: the score lexeme codes at deserialization, then the `hvVerdict` checks, then the order of policy ReviewValidation (architecture 5.2 RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand and 5.3 ReviewValidation), and the golden contract carries multi-violation cases. [S1 +S5 +S6 +S8]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-003-AC007 Validation runs before any mutation on every surface, including a review record carried in a turn body (submit, upsert, PATCH, PUT, complete, fail), which policy ReviewValidation checks with the same codes before the class and the completion gate are evaluated; score lexemes are validated at deserialization, before any lookup, so an invalid score on an unknown turn is 400, not 404. [S4 +S5 +S6]

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-004-AC001 `0.1234567890123456789` and `0.1234567890123456789012345678` round-trip unchanged through every hop: client JSON [S2], SQLite/PostgreSQL/SQL Server storage [S3], REST and MCP [S5], REPL YAML quoted/unquoted and JsonElement [S6], PowerShell plugin YAML block/flow and JSON [S8], the TypeScript-host adapters, which never parse a score [S9].

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-004-AC002 A JSON number or numeric string is accepted when its raw text matches `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$` (no sign, no exponent) with a value in [0,1] (`ScoreLexeme`, architecture 3.5.4); a normalized number (trailing fractional zeros stripped) is returned. [S1 +S2]

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-004-AC003 Validation runs on the raw lexeme before any numeric conversion, through the one rule `ScoreLexeme` (`ScoreLexemeJsonConverter` at deserialization on the server and client, the REPL normalizer, and the PowerShell core's `Protect-ReplLosslessScalars`, kept in step by the golden contract), so nothing is ever rounded: more than 28 fractional digits is rejected with `review_score_precision` (e.g. `0.12345678901234567890123456789`, which `JsonElement.TryGetDecimal` would round), exponent or signed forms with `review_score_format`, and values outside [0,1] with `review_score_out_of_range`; each case is tested as a JSON number, a JSON string, an unquoted YAML scalar, and a quoted YAML scalar. [S1 +S5 +S6 +S8]

Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005 Hostile validation receipt mapping. Scope (architecture 5.4, process ConvertHvReceiptToReview): the HostileReview subsystem (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001 to -006, its durable queue, its worker pinned to effort `xhigh`, and its AGREE, DISAGREE, or UNKNOWN verdicts) is separate from a turn's `hostileReview`; its results are not HV receipts for this record and never pass through this mapping. UC-7's live model and effort rule (gpt-6-astra, max) is an HV-protocol rule the coordinator checks from the reviewer's receipts before recording any verdict, not a plugin check.

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005-AC001 `accuracy/100` maps to `correctness` and `completeness/100` to `completeness` exactly. [S8]

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005-AC002 The plugins send the receipt's verdict as `hvVerdict` (AGREE or DISAGREE) with the mapped scores and no status, and the server maps it atomically at that write (policy HvVerdictMapping, architecture 5.3) with the hostile thresholds in force at that write, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver`. Before any mapping the server refuses an `hvVerdict` other than AGREE or DISAGREE with 400 `review_invalid_status` and `details.field` `hvVerdict`, an `hvVerdict` write missing either score with 400 `review_field_required_for_status` naming the missing score, and an `hvVerdict` sent with an explicit `status` with 400 `validation_error` and `details.field` `status`. The effective verdict is AGREE only when no reason starts with `FAIL:` or `UNKNOWN:`; otherwise the write maps as DISAGREE, the rule the plugin applies when it sets `hvVerdict` (AC003), so an MCP, client, or REPL caller and the plugin store the same status for the same fields (golden contract, C# and Pester). AGREE stores the derived Pass or Fail; DISAGREE stores Fail when the scores derive Fail, otherwise `Other` with a nonempty `otherNotes` chosen deterministically: the failed claims (FAIL entries of `reasons`) when present, otherwise the UNKNOWN claims, otherwise the verdict-level reason `DISAGREE with no listed failed or unknown claims` plus the response receipt path (`HvVerdictMappingDisagreeUnknownOnlyPassScoresOtherNamesUnknownClaims`, `HvVerdictMappingDisagreeNoListedClaimsPassScoresOtherVerdictLevelReason`). No client reads thresholds, and a mapped receipt never returns `review_status_conflict` (`HvVerdictMappingInstanceOverride095Scores097And099AgreeStoresPassDisagreeStoresOther`). `hvVerdict` travels unchanged through the client and the MCP tool (`HvVerdictClientAndMcpToolForwardedToServerMapping`, S5) and the REPL validator, schema, and flat-arg allow-list (`ReplRecordReviewHvVerdictValidatorSchemaFlatArgsForwarded`, S6). `hvReceiptPath` is owned by the plugin verbs (the PowerShell core, S8, for every host): the plugin reads and maps the receipt and sends the mapped fields with `hvVerdict`, and never forwards `hvReceiptPath` to the REPL, MCP tool, client, or server. `hvVerdict` on an agent review is refused with 400 `validation_error` and `details.field` `hvVerdict` (`SessionLogTurnReviewSectionTests.AgentReviewWithHvVerdictValidationError`, S4). [S4 +S5 +S6 +S8]

Rows.Domain: Turn reviews, scores, and thresholds
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005-AC003 `reasons` (each FAIL and UNKNOWN claim of the receipt, prefixed `FAIL:` or `UNKNOWN:`), the plugin sends `hvVerdict` AGREE only when the receipt's OverallVerdict is AGREE and every claim is PASS, otherwise DISAGREE (`HvReceiptAgreeWithFailOrUnknownClaimSentAsDisagree` in S8), `reviewedAt`, `reviewer` come from the receipt, and a DISAGREE receipt with empty FAIL and UNKNOWN lists and no `reasons` is valid input; the Codex HV receipt (the reviewer's JSON receipt and the `--json` response jsonl) is accepted as input. A receipt is refused by the plugin before any write with one code from the wire-contract error list naming the field: a verdict that is not AGREE or DISAGREE with `review_invalid_status` (field `hvVerdict`), a missing accuracy or completeness with `review_field_required_for_status` (field `correctness` or `completeness`), an accuracy or completeness outside 0..100 with `review_score_out_of_range`, and a jsonl path that does not exist with `review_receipt_paths_required` (field `requestJsonlPath` or `responseJsonlPath`) (`HvReceiptInvalidRefusedBeforeWriteExactCodes` and `HvReceiptDisagreeUnknownOnlyEmptyReasonsOtherNotesNamesUnknownClaims`, `HvReceiptDisagreeNoListedClaimsEmptyReasonsOtherNotesVerdictLevelReason` in S8); the server stores receipt paths as text without checking that they exist. [S8]

Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001 Review storage. AC-001 per-kind columns on `SessionLogTurns` (architecture 5.1: `Status` 16 required, `OtherNotes`, `Correctness`, `Completeness`, `CorrectnessThreshold`, `CompletenessThreshold` with `HasPrecision(29,28)`, `Reviewer` 256, `ReviewedAt` UTC, `RequestJsonlPath` and `ResponseJsonlPath` 2048); AC-002 `SessionLogTurnReviewReasons` table of `SessionLogTurnReviewReasonEntity { Id, WorkspaceId, SessionLogTurnId, Agent, SessionId, RequestId, Kind, Ordinal, Value }`, whose `Agent`, `SessionId`, and `RequestId` are its turn's key, copied from the turn in the same transaction, never changed, and in no key or index (architecture 3.1 "Root ids"); its wiki dump policy, `COPY-SANITIZE+HISTORY` listed with the session-log child tables, is FR-MCP-WIKIEXPORT-003's record and case (architecture 3.1 "Review reason dump policy" and 5.1, `WikiDumpReviewReasonsCopySanitizeHistory`, shared-platform domain); AC-003 the review part of the `_AddSessionLogTurnReviewsAndRequestClass` migration for each of the three providers, with the backfill of every existing row, soft-deleted rows included, and the database default `Unstarted` on each review `Status`, so a turn the prior binary inserts during a binary-only rollback reads as its `ReviewDefaults` after the roll-forward, which runs no second backfill; Up, Down, and Up on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server leave the schema and the data equal (architecture 5.1 and 8.5); AC-004 graph paths (stamp, detach, include, soft-delete, revive, transaction restore, federation). [S3 +S4]

Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002 DTOs and serialization. AC-001 the review DTOs `SessionLogTurnReviewKind`, `SessionLogTurnReviewInput`, and `SessionLogTurnReviewDto` are defined once, one type per file, in `src/QBrainAi.Client/Models/SessionLog/` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Models.SessionLog`) and the server uses them (no server copy), while `requestClass`, `agentReview`, and `hostileReview` are added to both develop definitions of `UnifiedRequestEntryDto` (`src/QBrainAi.Client/Models/SessionLogModels.cs:108`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Models/UnifiedSessionLogDto.cs:135` at `a8d3934b`), the one type kept twice, whose server and client parity is checked (architecture 3.5 and 5.1); AC-002 `ScoreLexemeJsonConverter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Scoring`, validating the lexeme at deserialization through `ScoreLexeme`, architecture 3.5.4) and the UTC converter; AC-003 source-gen registrations; AC-004 `TurnReadProjection` (architecture 3.5.3) is the read shape of every review: text through `SecretRedactor`, scores as exact lexemes, unset fields `null`, and its review-text redaction and the TR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001 decorator's review paths are the same `SecretRedactor` call (the component and its one rule set are TR-MCP-SHAREDPLATFORM-001 AC-006's); AC-005 the search text (`BuildSearchText`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/SessionLogService.cs:1367` at `a8d3934b`) includes reviewer, reasons, and otherNotes and excludes requestClass, scores, thresholds, and paths; the text filter runs over the raw stored turn, so a query for a raw value the sanitizer redacts in a review field still finds its turn, which reads back redacted (FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001 ac4 kept), and a reason present only in a replaced record no longer matches (architecture 3.4 Search and 5.2 QuerySessionLogsQuery: the former "a redacted review value matches no turn" clause is removed). [S1 +S2 +S4]

Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-003 Review units, sections, client, MCP tool. AC-001 `agentReview`/`hostileReview` sections (case-insensitive; aliases `agent-review`, `agent_review`, `hostile-review`, `hostile_review`) on `PUT` and `DELETE /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/sections/{section}` dispatch RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand and ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand, and a known non-review section stays on the existing handlers (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/SessionLogController.cs:576-601,606-628` at `a8d3934b`); AC-002 client `RecordTurnReviewAsync`/`ClearTurnReviewAsync`; AC-003 MCP `sessionlog_record_review(agent, sessionId, requestId, kind, reviewJson, workspacePath)`, which returns `{ success: true, review }`, and its descriptor JSON; MCP `sessionlog_replace_section` and `sessionlog_clear_section` called with a review section or alias dispatch RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand (reading `sectionJson` as the same `SessionLogTurnReviewInput`) and ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand, every non-review section keeps the direct service call (`FwhMcpTools.SessionLog.cs:203-253` at `a8d3934b`), the two tools' descriptions list the two review sections beside the nine they list today (`:203,231`; architecture 3.1 "Host details"), and `sessionlog_delete_item` on a review section is refused like the REST item route (`:256-279`); AC-004 every review refusal surfaces through the one `ClassifiedErrorException` branch of `McpErrorClassifier` (architecture 3.5.2: no per-feature branch): 400 with the review code in `code`, 422 `review_status_conflict` with the thresholds in force and the derived status in `details`, and on MCP `{ code, error, message, retryable, details }`, while an unresolved workspace is the shared 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `workspacePath` from WorkspaceResolutionBehavior after the dispatch (shared-platform domain; on REST the middleware answers first with its own body); AC-005 RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand and ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand (record and handler in two files each in `src/QBrainAi.Services/Reviews/Commands/`, namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Reviews.Commands`) delegate their save to `ISessionLogService.ReplaceTurnSectionAsync` and `ClearTurnSectionAsync` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/ISessionLogService.cs:108,121` at `a8d3934b`), which run `TurnLocator` and the save in one SerializableWrite with turn-level isolation inside the existing decorator chain (TR-SUPPORT-CORE-014 ac-5), so a review reset and a concurrent close of the same turn never both commit, and when the default bound (four attempts) is exhausted the unit returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing (architecture 5.2). [S4 +S5 +S10]

AC-001 `IReplJsonNumberNormalizer` (process PreserveReviewScoreLexemes, architecture 5.4) holds no lexeme rule: it calls `ScoreLexeme` for `correctness` and `completeness` inside `agentReview`, `hostileReview`, and `recordReview` and forwards each lexeme unchanged (the agent-context grade keys it also covers belong to the agent-context domain); AC-002 shapes, validator, schema JSON; AC-003 flat-arg allow-list and stateless dispatch; AC-004 workflow pre-check and revert; the pre-check is advisory like the plugin pre-check: it reports the missing items with the exact gate message as a warning and never refuses a close; a server gate refusal is surfaced with the server's message and missing items (`ReplPrecheckAdvisoryWarnsMissingItemsNeverRefuses`). AC-001 `Protect-ReplLosslessScalars` (the core's copy of the `ScoreLexeme` rule across the language boundary, kept in step by the golden contract); AC-002 `Invoke-WorkflowRecordReview` (no failsafe, including in a host session with `unsupportedSince`, where a review is refused and recorded after the drain through the original pair, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; every retryable answer, a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, is reported `persisted: false` with its code and `retryable: true`, exit 1, never `queued`, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002-AC005); AC-003 `ConvertFrom-McpHvReceipt` (process ConvertHvReceiptToReview, architecture 5.4: sets `hvVerdict` AGREE only when the receipt's OverallVerdict is AGREE and every claim is PASS, sends no `status`, never forwards `hvReceiptPath`); AC-004 advisory local pre-check that warns and never refuses (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004-AC002) and the stop-gate finding for a close the server refused with `session_turn_completion_gate` (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC003). AC-001 `ReviewDefaults` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Reviews`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Reviews/`, architecture 3.5.4) gives the default status for a kind and class and is applied at turn insert, by a section reset, by the Chore flip of policy RequestClassification (only a record still at a default status, only on a turn nonterminal before the write), and by the S3 backfill; AC-002 policy ReviewValidation (architecture 5.3), implemented by the S1 review validator seam, which calls `ScoreVerdict` for every derivation and holds no threshold comparison of its own, validates every review record: the RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand write (origin Agent) and each review a turn body carries through `TurnWritePipeline` (origins Agent, Import, and Replication), before policies RequestClassification and CompletionGate, returning the first violation in its fixed order. Rows.Text: FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 All agent plugins enforce the turn rules.

Rows.Domain: Plugin core runners and host adoption
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC001 The TypeScript hosts (cline, cline-v2, opencode) get every plugin behavior of this plan from the PowerShell core through the logic-free adapter (operator, 2026-10-11, PowerShell-only ruling): their host bindings satisfy exactly the ACs in the A8 allocation, including the stop-equivalent rules FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001, -AC002, -AC004, and -AC006 through cline-v2 `afterRun` and opencode `session.idle` through the `event` hook (in A8 driven through recorded host payload fixtures; the host repos run them in A9), and the adapter adds no behavior of its own: it forwards each host event the host binding table names (on opencode's `event` hook only an event of type `session.idle`) and each tool call to the PowerShell core and returns the core's result unchanged, so the structured failure cause (C9) of every core verb reaches the host as the core reports it. On a host whose stop-equivalent cannot hold the run open (P0.2 records it per host; architecture section 3.2, host limits (1), and process EvaluateStopGate), a block finding is recorded through `Update-TurnState` as `stop_gate_overridden_by_host` with the open turn ids and warned at the next prompt hook, because these hosts have no SessionStart event, and the feature matrix records the limitation (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC006; `TsHostStopEquivalentCannotBlockRecordsOverriddenByHostWarnsAtNextPrompt`). The required-memory block these hosts inject today (FR-MCP-MEMORY-007) comes from the PowerShell core: on cline-v2 through `beforeModel` and on opencode on the `chat.message` output, both forwarded by the adapter, and on classic cline as the `context_modification` output of its native UserPromptSubmit PowerShell hook (architecture section 3.2, host limits (3); `ClineUserPromptSubmitReturnsRequiredMemoriesAsContextModification`). The PowerShell core also carries the governed-host protections the approved plan gave the Node core (operator, 2026-10-12, round-2 finding R2-F10, verbatim answer "Port to PowerShell (Recommended)"): every core verb keeps the structured failure cause (`SessionVerbPreservesStructuredCauseC9`); a governed context uses only its bound REPL bridge, never an ambient HTTP fallback, and a missing bridge is a typed final failure (`GovernedContextNoAmbientHttpFallback`); a governed flush uses only the context-bound durable failsafe, keeps its pending, rejected, and quarantined completion blockers, and never replays a global or foreign-workspace failsafe; suppressing a flush is not audit clearance (`GovernedFlushContextBoundFailsafeOnlyNoForeignReplay`). [A8]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC004 Every host either has an arrival mechanism listed in the host binding table (operator D6) or reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing; no host relies on the model to open turns (cline-v2 is supported only when P0.2 shows one run per user message, and classic cline only for a task whose hook payload's `workspaceRoots` holds exactly one root, which is the mint's workspace, while a task with several roots is `turn_logging_unsupported` with zero mints and zero writes; architecture section 3.1, round-5 resolutions and "Host details"; P0.2 records the field; `ClineSingleWorkspaceRootIsMintWorkspace`, `ClineSeveralWorkspaceRootsTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites` in A8). A hook source that the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check cannot read (permissions, a policy directory) counts as a failing check, because the check must prove exactly one MCP prompt hook across every source (D11; `ClineUnreadableHookSourceFailsClosedTurnLoggingUnsupported` in A8, `CopilotUnreadableHookSourceFailsClosedTurnLoggingUnsupported` in A9). While the copilot or classic-cline duplicate check fails, every session-log verb of that plugin, not only its prompt hook, reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server; when the check starts failing in a host session after one of its requests was delivered, the first verb or hook that observes it records `unsupportedSince` with reason `duplicate_prompt_hook`, and writes for a turn already open go to the plugin failsafe (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001, `ClineDuplicateHookAfterDeliveryUnsupportedSinceOpenTurnCloseCaptured` for classic cline in A8, `DuplicateHookAfterDeliveryUnsupportedSinceOpenTurnCloseCaptured` for copilot in A9). [A8 +A9]

Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC005 All nine plugin versions are bumped to the one sync version, 1.120.0 (BUG-BUILD-008 lands at 1.119.0 first; architecture sections 8.4 and 8.5), and reported correctly by the marker `agent_plugins` section after a server restart. The marker generator (`MarkerFileService.BuildDefaultAgentPlugins`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/MarkerFileService.cs:532-611` at `a8d3934b`, five entries today) gains four contracts: `ClaudeCowork` (mcpserver-claude-cowork-plugin), `GrokBot` (mcpserver-grok-bot-plugin), `ClineV2` (mcpserver-cline-v2-plugin), and `OpenCode` (mcpserver-opencode-plugin), each with source type, plugin name, version read from that plugin's manifest, activation, startup command, required environment, hook and tool expectations, and root hints in the same shape as the existing five; P0.7 confirms each plugin's `PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME` and source type from its repository and records any difference as a RequirementRefined decision before A9; a marker read back after restart lists all nine with their bumped versions (`MarkerFileServiceAgentPluginsNineEntriesVersionsFromManifests`). The signed `agentPlugins.contractDigest` (`ComputeAgentPluginsDigest`, `MarkerFileService.cs:757-777` at `a8d3934b`, which hashes ten fields of every contract) then covers all nine contracts, so the digest value and the marker signature value change, while the signed field list (`SignaturePayloadFields`, `:50-83`) and the payload format of TR-MCP-SEC-005 stay as they are (`MarkerContractDigestCoversNineContractsSignedFieldListUnchanged`). Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC006 `docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md` lists, for each of the nine plugins and each turn-logging feature (ingress mint, arrival bridge or adapter, host-context binding, stop gate, session end), whether it is supported, adapted, or a documented capability limitation (D7) with the reason and the P0.2 receipt; every `turn_logging_unsupported` host appears there as a limitation. P0.8 writes it by restructuring today's eight-plugin feature grid (`docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md:20-46` at `a8d3934b`: no grok-bot, no receipts) into one row per plugin and feature, keeping its existing feature rows and bringing its "Primary Implementation" and "Test Framework" rows (`:42-43`, which name bash, Node, bats, and jest) to the PowerShell-only state. The host limits of architecture section 3.2 are rows, each with its P0.2 receipt: (1) stop gate: classic cline has no stop-equivalent, so the gate never runs there and its host sessions end only by the 12-hour idle rule, and cline-v2 `afterRun` and opencode `session.idle` evaluate and report but cannot hold the run open (`stop_gate_overridden_by_host`, AC001); (2) per-tool audit: not forwarded on cline-v2 (`beforeTool`, `afterTool`) or opencode (`tool.execute.before`, `.after`), because the PowerShell core has no tool-audit hook (`plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1:5` at `a8d3934b`), so these hosts match the PowerShell hosts and a tool audit stays with QB-AGENT-001's `tool_execution` work (C6); (3) required memories (FR-MCP-MEMORY-007): cline-v2 through `beforeModel`, opencode on the `chat.message` output, classic cline through its native hook's `context_modification`, with the explicit memory-list fallback where P0.2 shows that context does not reach the model; (4) classic cline tasks with several `workspaceRoots`: `turn_logging_unsupported` (AC004; architecture section 3.1, "Host details"); and session end on codex through the `session-end` wrapper the generator writes for codex's SessionEnd entry (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-009 AC-005). A host whose queued messages reach no arrival mechanism at enqueue is `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6; operator D5 requires minting at enqueue) with zero mints and writes until an enqueue adapter exists, and its row states that outcome; a P0.2 probe with outcome `unavailable` selects the row's stated default where one exists, and for an arrival mechanism selects D6 `turn_logging_unsupported` with reason "P0.2 unavailable", shown to the operator. The claude-code and claude-cowork rows also record the D6 limitation that an unattributable queue record (equal-content queued messages with no shared key) fails that host session closed for the rest of the session (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010). [A9]

Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 TypeScript-host bindings and the adapter contract in the PowerShell core (`plugins/core/lib-ps`; operator, 2026-10-11, PowerShell-only ruling; architecture section 3.2). AC-001 the cline, cline-v2, and opencode rows of the host binding table (nonces, host session keys, child-session marker, the `cl-` equal-field rule applied under the host session lock before the mint) are implemented in the PowerShell functions A3 and A4 own, and classic cline's native UserPromptSubmit command hook (`pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File <plugin root>/lib/plugin-hook.ps1 -HookName user-prompt-submit -HostName cline`) mints with the `cl-` nonce and the `taskId` key, takes the mint's workspace from the payload's `workspaceRoots` when it holds exactly one root and reports `turn_logging_unsupported` for a task with several (architecture section 3.1, "Host details"), and returns the required-memory block as the hook's `context_modification` output (`apps/vscode/proto/cline/hooks.proto:37-41` in the local Cline source at `b090c4a08`); AC-002 on hosts without a SessionStart event the first ingress event records the host session's `mcpSessionId` in `turn-state.yaml` under the host session lock before its mint; AC-003 the stop-equivalents (cline-v2 `afterRun`, opencode `session.idle` delivered through the `event` hook) run A7's Stop gate and never close a turn, and where the host's P0.2 row records that its stop-equivalent cannot hold the run open, a block finding is recorded as `stop_gate_overridden_by_host` with the open turn ids and warned at the next prompt hook (process EvaluateStopGate); AC-004 `lib/tool-descriptors.json` lists every tool the TypeScript hosts expose (the tools `plugins/core/lib-node/src/tools` exposes today, which P0.7 records; a tool with no PowerShell method is ported to one first), each with the `method` it runs through `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke` and its `mutates` flag, with review scores declared as strings; AC-005 each TypeScript host's adapter forwards each host hook the host binding table names (cline-v2 `beforeRun`, `beforeModel`, `afterRun`; opencode `chat.message`, `event`, `shell.env`, `experimental.chat.messages.transform`), as an argument list and never a shell string, to `lib/plugin-hook.ps1 -HostEvent <hook> -HostName <host> -WorkspacePath <the workspace directory the host's plugin API reports, recorded per host in P0.7>` with `{ input, output }` on stdin unchanged, returns a hook result where the host API takes a return object (cline-v2) as the host runtime's JSON parse of the object the core writes, never modified, and copies each property of the `output` object the core returns onto the host's output argument where the hook has one (opencode), forwards opencode's `event` hook only for an event whose `type` is `session.idle` and returns at once for any other type without starting `pwsh` (`OpenCodeEventHookOtherEventTypeNotForwardedNoPwshStart`), registers exactly the descriptors, forwards each tool call to `lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -WorkspacePath <dir> -InvocationFromStdin` with `{ params, hostContext }` on stdin, returns the core's stdout and exit status unchanged, returns the fixed failure `plugin_core_unavailable` when `pwsh` cannot be started or the event cannot be serialized, delivers tool arguments containing quotes, Unicode, and newlines to the core exactly on Linux and on Windows, and holds no other logic beyond its one fixed host-binding constant, the `session.idle` event type; AC-006 a write captured as `unsupported_session` on these hosts goes to the failsafe only and reaches no persistence path before its drain (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001); AC-007 the C2 alias journal's consumer interface in the PowerShell core (`sessions/<key>/aliases.yaml`): `Register-McpAliasConsumer -ConsumerId` (idempotent, persisted), `Get-McpUnacknowledgedAlias -ConsumerId`, `Get-McpAlias -Id` (either id resolves; `$null` when absent; `request_ambiguous` when ambiguous), and `Confirm-McpAliasAcknowledged -ConsumerId -PendingId` (idempotent), every alias stored as a permanent `lookup` entry `{ pendingId, requestId, aliasedAtUtc, acks }` with the root-id envelope, never pruned, and a prunable `delivery` entry `{ pendingId, requiredConsumers, acks }` whose required set is the consumers registered at its commit and which is pruned only when every member acknowledged, all bound to the immutable C4/C5 context of one host session; the TypeScript `createAliasService` interface agreed on 2026-10-09 is withdrawn by the ruling, and this PowerShell interface is posted to QB-AGENT-001 as a CONTRACT entry (no exactly-once delivery claim); AC-008 `plugin-hook.ps1 -HostEvent <name> -HostName <host>` maps each host event the host binding table names to its canonical hook (cline-v2 `beforeRun` and opencode `chat.message` to `user-prompt-submit`, whose returned opencode `output` also carries the `REQUIRED MEMORIES` block of FR-MCP-MEMORY-007, cline-v2 `beforeModel` to the required-memory handler, which returns the model request with that block added unless the request already carries it, and in `Stateless` mode, where cline-v2's P0.2 row (probe (j)) records that the returned request replaces the model's messages, also applies the history-exclusion handler of RunStatelessInvocation (both render the block with the one core renderer `plugins/core/lib-ps/memory-context.ps1`, architecture section 3.1, "Required-memory renderer"), cline-v2 `afterRun` to `stop-gate`, opencode `event` to `stop-gate` when `event.type` is `session.idle` (session key `event.properties.sessionID`) and to an exit-0 no-op for every other event type (a defense, because the adapter forwards no other type), opencode `shell.env` to the shell-environment handler that returns `MCP_HOST_SESSION_KEY` from `input.sessionID`, and opencode `experimental.chat.messages.transform` to the history-exclusion handler of RunStatelessInvocation) and refuses any other event with `host_event_unknown`, writing nothing; AC-009 `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -InvocationFromStdin` reads `{ params, hostContext }` as UTF-8 JSON from stdin, binds `params` exactly as `-ParamsObject` would, and derives the host session key from `hostContext` per the host binding table (opencode `sessionID`, cline-v2 `conversationId`), never from `params` (`TsAdapterTwoSessionsIdenticalArgsDistinctHostSessionKeys`), and both it and `plugin-hook.ps1 -HostEvent` read stdin as UTF-8 regardless of the console code page, Windows included (`CoreStdinUtf8IndependentOfConsoleCodePage`, run on Linux and on Windows); AC-010 every core verb keeps the structured failure cause of a response (detail code and retryable flag, `classified-error.ps1`) and never reduces it to a string, so C9 detail codes such as `mint_collision_exhausted`, and a 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, which the core handles as an outage (architecture section 3.1, "Deadlock and busy outcomes"), reach the caller with their flags; AC-011 a governed context (a host-selected, absolute REPL executable bound to the invocation context) uses only that bound bridge and never an ambient HTTP or REST fallback for its verbs (session log, TODO, requirements, triage), and a missing bridge is a typed final failure; the marker trust check's read-only health and nonce request (`plugins/core/lib-ps/marker-resolver.ps1:218` at `a8d3934b`) is not a verb fallback and stays (architecture section 3.1, "Governed verbs and the trust check"), so `GovernedContextNoAmbientHttpFallback` drives the verbs only; AC-012 a governed flush uses only the context-bound durable failsafe, keeps its pending, rejected, and quarantined completion blockers (C3, C8), and never replays a global or foreign-workspace failsafe directory through a governed bridge; suppressing a flush is not audit clearance (AC-010..AC-012 (operator, 2026-10-12, round-2 finding R2-F10, verbatim answer "Port to PowerShell (Recommended)")). [A8]

Rows.Domain: Context packages and token budget
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001 Context package construction and provenance: for the session-log turn named by `agent`, `sessionId`, and `requestId` (TurnLocator), the server builds a bounded, reproducible package from the request, the canonical profile and rules (`ProfileSources`, `RuleSources`), the applicable requirements (those linked to the turn's TODO, an `ISSUE-<n>` id included, plus those linked to the turn by relationships or named in `focusRefs`; a turn whose `todoId` is `None` has only the latter two, architecture 3.1, Applicable requirements), related turns (never the request's own turn), TODOs, receipts, trusted fresh prior responses, and code at the workspace HEAD commit; it records each item's source hash over the stored normal form (ContentHasher), the commit, the selection rationale, token usage, contradiction and blocker findings, every omitted candidate with its reason, and an immutable input snapshot; it redacts secrets before anything is stored (SecretRedactor); it links the package `derived_from` each included source and `relevant_to` its turn in the package's own transaction, and those links are protected (a Rule file outside version control is provenance only, never a link or a staleness dependency); and it replays the package identically from that snapshot only, never from live sources, configuration, relationships, or response statuses. A repeated idempotency key with equal client inputs returns the stored package before any source is read, and with other inputs is 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`. Packages are readable in every Mode. The record states, as a glossary entry, that a context package is not FR-SUPPORT-010's context pack (ranked context chunks for a query) and cites FR-MCP-082's bounded TODO execution context as related and not reused (architecture 6.1). Units: BuildAgentContextPackageCommand, GetAgentContextPackageQuery, QueryAgentContextPackagesQuery, ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery (architecture 6.5).

Rows.Domain: Context packages and token budget
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-002 Token budget and explicit overflow: token counts are the deterministic estimate `ceil(utf8ByteCount / BytesPerToken)` per item, and the request's optional `tokenBudget` (from 1024 up to the configured `TokenBudget`) narrows the budget; mandatory context (the request, profile, rules, and applicable requirements) is never truncated and never cut by the candidate limits; mandatory tokens equal to the budget build, and one token more fails the build with 422 `agent_context_budget_exceeded` (`details { tokenBudget, mandatoryTokenCount, overflowTokenCount, mandatoryItems }`) and stores an `Overflow` package with its mandatory items, token counts, and input snapshot and no content; optional candidates fill the remaining budget in rank order (a candidate whose tokens equal the remainder is included), each kind capped at `MaxCandidatesPerKind` (`PriorResponse` at `MaxPriorResponses`), the rest omitted with reason `budget` or `below_candidate_limit`; a repeated or concurrent build with the same key and client inputs returns the same 422 with the stored diagnostics, never a package; in `Pilot` and `Stateless` the failure fails the invocation (FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009). Unit: BuildAgentContextPackageCommand with the nested activity FillBudgetWithCandidates (architecture 6.2, 6.5).

the entities `AgentContextPackageEntity`, `AgentContextPackageItemEntity`, `AgentContextPackageFocusRefEntity`, `AgentContextPackageInputEntity`, `AgentContextPackageInputLinkEntity`, `AgentContextOmissionEntity`, and `AgentContextFindingEntity` in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/AgentContext/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Entities.AgentContext`; composite keys with `WorkspaceId`, root ids on every child row, registered by StorageSchema); the request and result DTOs in `src/QBrainAi.Client/Models/AgentContext/` (`QBrainAi.Client.Models.AgentContext`); keys `pkg-<requestId>-<nn>` from ReadableKeyAllocator; IdempotentCreate with policy `Conflict` over `PayloadSha256` of the client inputs, looked up read-only before any source read; the reads (ReadBuildInputs) before a database-only SerializableWrite whose delegate re-checks the turn status, each attempt under `StorageCommandBudget.Default` (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/StorageCommandBudget.cs:12` at `a8d3934b`), whose expiry is the 503 `backend_unavailable` storage answer; Rows.Domain: Responses, grading, trust, and response lifecycle
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-003 Response submission: in `Pilot` and `Stateless` the model submits its response with the `agent_context_submit_response` tool before it closes the turn, and the plugin supplies the request's `packageId` (FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009). A submission answers a `Built` package (BuiltPackageLookup: an unknown package is 404 `not_found` `package`, an `Overflow` package 409 `agent_context_package_overflow`) and carries `agent` (equal to the package's), `model`, `effort`, `invocationMode` (`Stateless` only for a package built in `Stateless`), the content, at least one claim, and for every claim at least one evidence item of kind `File`, `Requirement`, `Receipt`, `Commit`, or `SessionLogTurn` that never names the request's own turn and, except `Commit`, names an existing source; each refusal is 400 `validation_error` naming the field. The server computes each evidence hash at submission through SourceResolver (`File` at its `commitSha`, by default the workspace HEAD commit; an unreadable commit is 409 `agent_context_commit_unavailable`) and keeps the cited hash beside it, so a wrong cited hash stays a deterministic FAIL; it redacts the content and hashes its stored normal form (`ContentSha256`); it stores the response `Submitted` under `rsp-<requestId>-<nn>` with its claims, its evidence, the package's root ids, and its protected `derived_from` and `supports` links, all in one transaction. A repeated idempotency key returns the stored response only for an identical whole submission (`SubmissionSha256`); any differing input is 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`. Responses stay readable in every Mode and each read reports the effective status (FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-005). Units: SubmitAgentResponseCommand with the nested activity ReadSubmissionInputs, GetAgentResponseQuery, QueryAgentResponsesQuery (architecture 6.3, 6.4, 6.5).

Rows.Domain: Responses, grading, trust, and response lifecycle
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-004 Grading, HV requests, and trust: every response is graded by deterministic evidence checks and by the configured independent model grader. The deterministic grade (re-run on request) records one finding per evidence item (PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN by kind; `Commit` by ancestry of the response's commit, UNKNOWN without a git checkout) and the global findings (every claim evidenced, no secret, the response fresh), with correctness PASS over PASS plus FAIL (0 when nothing could be evaluated) and completeness the share of claims whose every check passes. The model grade is recorded by the HV agent in a grade-only continuation of its own reviewer thread after the runner froze its review receipts, for the responses of an HV request that names a range of session-log turns (no grading worker or HV pipeline in this effort, operator 2026-10-11); it is accepted only from the configured grader (`ModelGrader:*`, default Codex `gpt-6-astra` `max`; otherwise 403 `agent_context_grader_not_allowed`), only with its receipt paths and reviewer ids (400 `agent_context_receipt_paths_required`), only for a gradable response (409 `agent_context_response_not_gradable` for `Rejected` or `Superseded`) that is an item (409 `agent_context_grade_not_in_hv_request`) of an open HV request (409 `agent_context_hv_request_closed`), and only after the eight checks of architecture 6.3 pass (`receipt_path`, `request_meta`, `verdict_block`, `verdict_binding`, `verdict_match`, `reviewer_turn`, `reviewer_independent`, `runtime_identity`; otherwise 422 `agent_context_receipt_unverified` naming the check); an equal resubmission returns the stored grade and a different one is 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`. Each grade unit runs its read-only checks, then dispatches EvaluateStalenessCommand for its response, then saves in one SerializableWrite that re-checks the response's `StatusVersion` and dispatches the internal trust decision (DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand: no surface, not mode-gated, reads only the database). "Latest" means the greatest server-stamped `RecordedUtc`, then `GradeId`; a client `gradedUtc` is provenance only. A response is `Trusted` only when it is fresh, neither `Rejected`, `Stale`, nor `Superseded`, and the verdicts of its latest deterministic and latest model grade, re-derived from their stored scores and counts at `max(configured now, 0.98)`, are both `Pass` with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN findings; otherwise it is `Grading`, and a trust threshold below 0.98 fails startup. An HV request (`hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>`, idempotent by key) lists only the gradable responses of its range (400 `agent_context_hv_request_invalid` for an unknown session, a bad range, a range over `HvRequest:MaxTurns`, or none gradable), each `Pending` in at most one open request; an item closes when its response is rejected or superseded, the request completes when no item is `Pending`, and a rerun of an abandoned review grades the remaining items. The model grader and its option set are separate from the hostile-review worker of FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 (effort `xhigh`), and an HV request is not a request of the FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW queue (architecture 6.1). Units: RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand with the nested activity ReadModelGradeInputs, DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery (architecture 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5).

Rows.Domain: Responses, grading, trust, and response lifecycle
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-005 Rejection, staleness, and supersession: rejected, stale, and superseded responses are preserved for audit and never retrieved as trusted context. Every status change follows the response lifecycle of architecture 6.3 through ResponseStatusTransition: a repeat of an applied transition returns 200 unchanged, a transition the lifecycle does not draw is 409 `agent_context_transition_invalid` (a reject of a `Superseded` response, a supersede of a `Rejected` original or of one superseded by another response), and in the same transaction a response leaving `Trusted` marks its GraphRAG projection row and a reject or supersede closes the response's `Pending` HV items. A supersede names a replacement for the same request that is neither `Rejected` nor `Superseded` and closes no cycle (otherwise 409 `agent_context_supersede_invalid`), and it is the only writer of a `supersedes` link. A response is stale when a dependency changed: the `depends_on`, `derived_from`, and `supports` targets of the response and of its package, its evidence (including evidence outside its package), and every cited requirement (stale when deleted or superseded), with files compared at the workspace HEAD commit (an uncommitted edit changes nothing, a file absent at HEAD has changed), and never the request's own turn or a Rule file outside version control; a requirement's hash covers the effective record's id, title, description, and acceptance-criterion texts in order, never its status, its criteria's satisfaction flags or evidence, or timestamps, so recording a criterion satisfied or an HV verdict stales nothing (architecture 3.1, Requirement hash). Only EvaluateStalenessCommand persists `Stale` (ids validated and selected by ResponseIdList, unknown ids returned in `notFound`); every read that returns or counts a response's status (the response reads, retrieval, the status query, and the pilot report) reports the effective status and writes nothing. After the commit of each requirement write that changes or deletes a requirement or its acceptance criteria, the requirement service dispatches EvaluateStalenessCommand for the responses that cite a changed requirement (and, after a change of the current requirement layer, with no `responseIds`), only while Mode is not `Off`, outside the requirement transaction, and a failed or exhausted dispatch is logged and never fails the requirement write (architecture 3.1, Requirement writes and staleness). A unit that marks a projection row (the grade units through the trust decision, Reject, Supersede, EvaluateStalenessCommand) dispatches the projection pass after its commit (FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-007). Units: RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand with the nested activity EvaluateOneResponseStaleness, and the freshness rule of GetAgentResponseQuery and QueryAgentResponsesQuery (architecture 3.5.5, 6.3, 6.5).

Rows.Domain: Relationships, retrieval, and GraphRAG projection
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-006 Typed relationships: packages, responses, requirements, turns, TODOs, code files, receipts, profile files, and rule files (the `SourceKind` wire values `Package`, `Response`, `Requirement`, `SessionLogTurn`, `Todo`, `CodeFile`, `Receipt`, `Profile`, `Rule`) are linked with `implements`, `verifies`, `depends_on`, `supports`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`, `blocks`, `derived_from`, and `relevant_to`. Both refs resolve through SourceResolver, and the target's hash (`ToSha256`), read before the write, is kept on the link for staleness; a ref that names no existing source is 400 `validation_error` naming `fromRef` or `toRef`, an unknown kind or type or a self-link is 400 `agent_context_relationship_invalid`, and a client request for type `supersedes` is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `type`, because only SupersedeAgentResponseCommand writes the supersede chain. An identical link, created again or concurrently, returns the stored link with `created: false`; a deleted identical link is revived with its `RelationshipId` and `created: true`. Every link a command made (Build's `derived_from` and `relevant_to`, Submit's `derived_from` and `supports`, Supersede's `supersedes`) is protected (409 `agent_context_relationship_protected`); a client-made link of any type can be deleted (soft delete, 204). Links are queried by node, type, and direction (`out`, `in`, `both`) with bounded paging. The record states why the links are one store of their own, beside `GraphRelationshipEntity`, `TodoRequirementLinkEntity`, `RequirementTraceabilityLinkEntity`, `MemoryEdgeEntity` (TR-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL-002), and `HostileReviewArtifactLinkEntity`, and that an identical link returns `created: false` where a duplicate memory edge is 409 (architecture 6.3). Units: CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand, DeleteAgentContextRelationshipCommand, QueryAgentContextRelationshipsQuery (architecture 6.5).

Rows.Domain: Relationships, retrieval, and GraphRAG projection
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-007 GraphRAG projection with deterministic fallback: trusted responses are projected into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval and removed when they stop being trusted. A projection pass (ProjectAgentResponsesCommand, gated like every agent-context command) runs on request and as the background pass: the unit whose transaction marked a projection row (the grade units through the trust decision, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand) dispatches it with no `responseIds` after its commit, and a failed dispatch is logged and never fails that unit (architecture 3.1, Projection pass). The pass first persists each selected response's staleness (EvaluateStalenessCommand), then ingests a `Trusted` response into `GraphRagStorageScope.Workspace` only, when its projected hash differs (title the `responseId`, `sourceType` `agent-response`, `sourceKey` `agent-context/<responseId>`, so a hit maps back to its response), and deletes the document of a response that is no longer `Trusted`; `GraphRag:ProjectionEnabled` false skips ingest only, GraphRAG disabled skips ingest and keeps a removal `Pending` until GraphRAG is enabled, an ingest or delete error is `Failed` with `LastError` and retried on the next pass, and each row is saved through SerializableWrite with the response status re-read after the GraphRAG call (projection row states, architecture 6.3). Retrieval (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery, readable in every Mode) takes the GraphRAG path only when `preferGraphRag` asks for it, `GraphRag:UseForRetrieval` allows it, and only `PriorResponse` is requested; that path keeps one workspace-scoped hit per response that is `Trusted` and fresh; any other case answers from the deterministic relational path with the stated `fallbackReason` (`graphrag_disabled`, `graphrag_not_initialized`, `graphrag_not_indexed`, `index_in_progress`, `retrieval_disabled`, `graphrag_error`, `graphrag_kinds_unsupported`), which ranks by the relationship neighborhood of the turn (`agent`, `sessionId`, `requestId`, never itself a candidate) and the focus refs the request names, or by the existing hybrid search (FR-MCP-004) when it names neither, a hit mapping by its document's source type to a `CodeFile` (`repo`) or `SessionLogTurn` (`session-log`) candidate and every other source type dropped (architecture 3.1, Hybrid-search hits as candidates); every `PriorResponse` candidate is checked for staleness read-only and nothing is written. Units: RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery, ProjectAgentResponsesCommand with the nested activity ProjectOneResponse (architecture 6.3, 6.5).
