Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-008 Surfaces: every externally callable agent-context unit (GetAgentContextStatusQuery, BuildAgentContextPackageCommand, GetAgentContextPackageQuery, QueryAgentContextPackagesQuery, ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery, SubmitAgentResponseCommand, GetAgentResponseQuery, QueryAgentResponsesQuery, RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand, CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand, DeleteAgentContextRelationshipCommand, QueryAgentContextRelationshipsQuery, RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery, ProjectAgentResponsesCommand, GetAgentContextPilotReportQuery, CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery) is available, dispatching the same record through `IDispatcher`, through REST (`AgentContextController` under `/qbrainai/agent-context` and the alias `/mcpserver/agent-context`), the MCP tools `agent_context_*` (`workspacePath` first; the unit's result DTO as camelCase JSON, or `{ code, error, message, retryable, details }`), the typed client (`QBrainAiClient.AgentContext`), the REPL (`client.AgentContext.<Method>`, bound by parameter name through `GenericClientPassthrough`), and, in all nine plugins, the PowerShell builders `New-McpAgentContext<Verb>Params` and one `agent_context_*` tool descriptor per unit (the TypeScript hosts through their adapters). Every error is the unit's listed code in the `ClassifiedError` body (a workspace that does not resolve is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `workspacePath`, an unknown route id 404 `not_found` naming the resource, a paging value outside its bounds 400 naming the field). The REPL's `agentContext` client namespace is service-gated with its eleven query methods on the read list: a read is never refused, and a command is refused in the REPL with `transaction_degraded` while the turn transaction coordinator is degraded and allowed while required turn transactions are active (updates FR-MCP-120 and TR-MCP-TXN-001). The hosted agent's generic `mcp_client_invoke` reaches `client.AgentContext.*` under the same units, Mode gate, and REPL client policy as any agent, cannot record a model grade (only the configured grader can), and the ACID profile is unchanged (architecture 3.1, Hosted agents). The two internal units have no endpoint by design: DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand (the trust decision, run inside RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand) and process RunStatelessInvocation (the plugin's stateless invocation, run by the plugins' prompt hooks) (architecture 6.4, 6.5).

Rows.Domain: Agent-context surfaces, mode, and stateless invocation
Rows.Text: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009 Opt-in mode, stateless invocation, and pilot: `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode` is `Off` by default, and stateful behavior stays the default until the operator changes it from the pilot report. The server reads the Mode at each dispatch, so a reloaded configuration takes effect without a restart (architecture 3.1, Mode at runtime). In `Off` every gated agent-context command (every command except the internal trust decision carries the marker) answers 409 `agent_context_disabled` while the status query and every read-only query stay available for audit; `Pilot` builds, records, and grades packages without injecting them; `Stateless` gives the model only the rendered package, the current request, and the host's deterministic `REQUIRED MEMORIES` block, with the messages of earlier requests excluded and, on each later model call of the same request's tool loop, that request's own prompt, tool calls, and results kept (architecture 3.1, Tool loops in `Stateless`), on a host whose P0.2 row records an authoritative history-exclusion operation, and any other host runs `Stateless` as `Pilot` with its feature-matrix limitation; a host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt, or runs the prompt anyway after a hook timeout, crash, or `plugin_core_unavailable`, runs `Pilot` and `Stateless` as `Off`. The plugin reads the Mode at host session start through GetAgentContextStatusQuery (at the first prompt on cline, cline-v2, and opencode), caches it for the host session, treats an unreadable or unknown Mode as `Off`, caches `Off` and continues statefully when a build or submission answers 409 `agent_context_disabled`, and applies a change away from `Off` at the next host session start. For a delivered request (on claude-code and claude-cowork after syncing the transcript to take the bridge-minted request id; an absorbed mid-turn message runs as `Pilot`) the plugin builds the package with the request id as idempotency key and keeps its `packageId` in the per-turn file; any build error or outage (the REPL's `transaction_degraded` and `mutation_not_transactional` included), a success whose package is not `Built`, or a pending mint fails the invocation (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation"): the prompt is refused with the code and message (and the token counts of an overflow), no answer is produced, and the plugin closes the request's own turn `canceled` with `failureNote` `agent_context_invocation_failed <code>: <message>` (the only `canceled` a hook writes, updating FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001 `ac-2`), held in the failsafe on an outage while the Stop gate warns; a final mint refusal, a hook that mints nothing, and a bridge request with no enqueue record leave no turn, so the prompt is refused with no close (for a final mint refusal the Stop gate warns, naming the prompt, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008). The model submits its response with `agent_context_submit_response` before it closes the turn, the plugin supplying the `packageId` (found again by request id when lost) and then requesting the deterministic grade; a missing submission is not a Stop-gate item. The pilot report compares responses by `invocationMode` with counts by effective status, means over model-graded responses, and the trust rate, and counts `Overflow` packages, packages without a response, and refused prompts. Units: GetAgentContextStatusQuery, GetAgentContextPilotReportQuery, process RunStatelessInvocation with the nested activities FailInvocation and AnswerAndSubmit (architecture 3.1, 6.2, 6.4, 6.5, 6.6).

Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-SHAREDPLATFORM-001 Shared storage, paging, redaction, and hashing components (architecture 3.5.2; owner SharedComponents; mapped to FR-MCP-105, the FR of the storage-integrity TRs TR-MCP-DB-001..006, because every unit writes and reads its stored records through these components). Files and namespaces: `DbErrorClassifier` in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Errors/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Errors`), `SerializableWrite` in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Transactions/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Transactions`), `IdempotentCreate` and `PayloadFingerprint` in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Idempotency/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Idempotency`), `ReadableKeyAllocator` in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Keys/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Keys`), `PagedQuery` and `PageBounds` in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Paging/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Paging`) with `PageResult<TItem>` in `src/QBrainAi.Client/Paging/` (`QBrainAi.Client.Paging`), `SecretRedactor` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/Redaction/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Redaction`), and `ContentHasher` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/Hashing/` (`QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Hashing`). AC-001 `DbErrorClassifier.IsUniqueViolation(exception, out indexName)` recognizes SQL Server 2601 and 2627, PostgreSQL 23505, and SQLite 2067 and 1555, and `IsTransientConflict(exception)` recognizes SQL Server 1205, PostgreSQL 40001 and 40P01, and SQLite 5 and 6, each by provider code; a timeout or transport failure is never a transient conflict (`HandoffDbExceptions.IsCommitAmbiguous`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/HandoffDbExceptions.cs:49` at `a8d3934b`, keeps its meaning), and new code never calls develop's message-text predicates (`SessionLogService.cs:234,357,812-817`) (`DbErrorClassifierProviderCodesTimeoutNeverTransient`, named here, one theory row per provider code); AC-002 `SerializableWrite` runs a unit's checks and save as one delegate in one Serializable transaction on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server, so a concurrent write to the same entity commits wholly before or after it (`SerializableWriteForcedInterleavingTestEntityCommitsWhollyBeforeOrAfter`, on a test entity SharedComponents owns, three providers); a transient conflict or a unique violation on a key the delegate declares rolls the transaction back and reruns the whole delegate at most three times (four attempts) unless the caller states its own bound and exhaustion outcome, then the unit answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing (`SerializableWriteRetriesExhausted409ConflictRetryableNothingSaved`, three providers); a refusal the delegate returns rolls back and is returned unchanged; a command dispatched inside the delegate joins the caller's transaction and retry and never opens a second one; per-response writes increment each named response's `StatusVersion` in ascending `ResponseId` order as the transaction's first statements; on the EF in-memory provider the delegate runs once with no transaction, as develop does (`SessionLogService.cs:155`), and a caller-owned transaction is refused as develop refuses it (`SessionLogService.cs:119-128`) (`SerializableWriteInMemoryRunsOnceCallerTransactionRefused`, named here; the turn-write units keep develop's own cases for both rules, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-007, domain Turn persistence); AC-003 `IdempotentCreate` runs inside SerializableWrite and looks its key up before any precondition that can change between attempts; `PayloadFingerprint` is SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the client-supplied inputs only, never over server-observed sources; an equal fingerprint returns the stored record with `created: false`, and another follows the caller's stated policy, `Conflict` (409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`), `ReturnStored`, or `MergeInto`; a unique violation on the key index ends the attempt, and the rerun's lookup finds the winner (`IdempotentCreateMismatchPoliciesConcurrentDuplicateFindsWinner`, named here; precedent `TodoPayloadFingerprint`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TodoPayloadFingerprint.cs:10`, and TR-HANDOFF-TODO-001); its soft-delete revive is TR-MCP-DB-003-AC001; AC-004 `ReadableKeyAllocator` allocates `NextOrdinal` keys (`<prefix>-<parent>-<nn>`: the suffix has at least two digits, starts at 01, is one more than the highest stored suffix for that prefix in the workspace compared as a number, and widens past 99) and `RandomHex` keys (`req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`, the Phase A minter); a key longer than 128 characters shortens its embedded parent id by the rule of architecture 6.3 while the full root ids stay in their own columns; every key is per workspace, so two workspaces holding the same parent id get the same key string with no collision; a collision on the key's unique index declares a retry to SerializableWrite with the next candidate, under SerializableWrite's default bound and its 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, except that the Phase A minter states its own bound for a collision of its random request id only (six attempts, then 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`) (`ReadableKeyAllocatorRandomHexRequestIdFormatCollisionNextCandidate`, named here; `ReadableKeyAllocatorMaxLengthRootIdsFitAndStayDistinct`, three providers; `ReadableKeyAllocatorShortRootIdsKeepFullReadableForm`; `ReadableKeyAllocatorSameParentIdTwoWorkspacesSameKeyNoCollisionNoExhaustion`; `ReadableKeyAllocatorSuffixPast99WidensLatestGradeOrderKept`, at ResponsesAndTrust's gate because it needs that context's types, architecture 3.1 "Test placement"); its soft-deleted suffix rule is TR-MCP-DB-003-AC002; Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-CQRS-001 (TR:696) "Standalone CQRS Library". Changes: the statement adds that `IDispatcher` is registered scoped, as a facade that resolves the handler and every behavior from the DI scope it was itself resolved in and runs them through the singleton `Dispatcher` (which keeps its logger-provider and active-dispatch bookkeeping), in place of today's singleton registration that resolves transient handlers from the root provider (`src/QBrainAi.Cqrs/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:22-27`, `src/QBrainAi.Cqrs/Dispatcher.cs:17,93,96`); the scope is the caller's (the HTTP request scope on REST and MCP Streamable HTTP, the MCP server's per-call scope on stdio through `McpServerOptions.ScopeRequests`, default on, and a scope a hosted service or the stdio host's startup work creates, `McpStdioHost.cs:340`); Phase 2 keeps today's registration and SharedComponents changes it (architecture 8.2); the published `QBrainAI.Cqrs` takes a major version for it (architecture 8.1: a consumer that resolves `IDispatcher` from the root provider or injects it into a singleton fails under DI scope validation, inference), and no `src` singleton injects `IDispatcher` at `a8d3934b` (its five users are `MemoryController`, `ProductsController`, `UseCasesController`, `FwhMcpTools.Memory.cs`, and the scoped `TransactionGatedMemoryService`, `Program.cs:484`). The stored status text "complete - 37 unit tests passing" is not one of the four statuses the REPL validator writes (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/ReplYamlMessageValidator.cs:639`), so the update sends status `pending`. New AC: TR-MCP-CQRS-001-AC001 a dispatch made inside a handler or inside a SerializableWrite delegate shares the caller's `McpDbContext` and transaction, two parallel requests for two workspaces share no `McpDbContext`, and the existing UseCases, Products, Memory, and GraphRAG suites pass unchanged through the production composition of both roots [SharedPlatform].

Rows.Text: - TR-MCP-NUKE-003 Plugin sync: version, receipt, parent resolution, lockfiles, PowerShell-only scope, and the open-turn cache guard (Nuke `SyncAgentPlugins`, process SyncAgentPluginsAtVersion, architecture 4.4; implementation detail of FR-MCP-BUILD-001, no TEST record; operator, 2026-10-10; context BuildTooling). The `--plugin-version` parameter is new (develop computes the next minor version, `build/Build.SyncAgentPlugins.cs:63,89-111` at `a8d3934b`, and keeps doing so when the parameter is absent); this plan syncs once at `--plugin-version 1.120.0`, after the named prerequisite BUG-BUILD-008 has landed at 1.119.0, the version its unpushed branches of eight plugin repos and three installed caches already carry (architecture 8.4 and 8.5). Each repo the sync writes passes the packaged-path check `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnlyPackage` (`:244-245,405-433`), which all nine pass, and the core integrity check (`:244,387-403`, `plugins/core/sync/check-core-integrity.ps1`), which fails on any file `CORE-MANIFEST.yaml` lists whose SHA-256 differs; so a repo whose synced builders, tool descriptors, or other core files differ fails at its own sync step, while the receipt of AC-002 names `lib/plugin-hook.ps1` as the architecture states (this reconciles whatif-c.md WC-M14 with architecture 4.4; inference: the sync writes the manifest from the source files it copies). The sync ends by refreshing the installed host caches of the synced version (`RefreshKnownPluginCaches`, `:71,652-662`, develop behavior, kept), so it runs only at rollout and as a same-version re-sync, never in a gate (architecture 8.4). AC-001 `SyncAgentPlugins` syncs lib-ps to all nine hosts, the three TypeScript hosts included, and packs nothing (operator, 2026-10-11, PowerShell-only ruling), so it no longer calls `RefreshNodePluginCoreVendorPackages` (`:61`), writing the explicit, idempotent `--plugin-version` to all nine (a re-run at the same version refreshes the synced content and changes no version), and, for a TypeScript host that P0.7 records as loading compiled output, running that host's existing `npm run build` to compile its adapter (a build step of the sync, never a test); AC-002 a run fails when its receipt does not list exactly the nine repos or does not show every host at the target version with the `lib/plugin-hook.ps1` SHA-256 of `plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1`; AC-003 the default plugin parent is TR-MCP-NUKE-006's `ResolveOfficialPluginSiblingParent`; without `--agent-plugin-parent`, a root with no sibling plugin repos finds none and fails the run (today the target logs a warning and returns, `:49-54`), and with the flag all nine are found; AC-004 the sync changes a TypeScript host's `package-lock.json` only by running npm in that host, never by writing or re-serializing the file itself, so `RewriteVersionedJson` no longer rewrites lockfiles and the version plan holds no lockfile (`:262,289,320-334,352`): the one-time removal of the packed-core dependency runs `npm uninstall` of that package in the host, and a version bump goes through `npm version <version> --no-git-tag-version`; after a sync `npm ci` succeeds in every TypeScript host and `npm install --package-lock-only` leaves its lockfile unchanged (operator, 2026-10-10: "Never edit an npm lockfile.  It belongs to npm.  If you want it changed, use npm."; BUG-BASELINE-012 found the 2026-10-01 sync leaving a stale integrity that `npm ci` rejected, fixed with `npm update @sharpninja/mcpserver-plugin-core`); AC-005 `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnly` (`:75-87`) applies an extension rule to every tracked path (`git ls-files`) of each of the nine repos, `tests/` included: on a TypeScript host it allows only the adapter entry file `src/index.ts` (the source of the `main: dist/index.js` that every TypeScript host's `package.json` names), `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`, and the npm-owned lockfile; the git-ignored `dist/` may hold only the compiler output of that entry file (`index.js`, `index.d.ts`, and their `.map` files) from the host's existing `npm run build` (`tsc`), and the git-ignored `node_modules/` holds installed dependencies, which are not plugin code and are not scanned; any other bats, bash, Node, TypeScript, or Python file fails the run; its content rule (the forbidden-reference scan, `:477-500`) covers only the packaged paths `lib/`, `hooks/`, `skills/`, `plugin.json`, and `CORE-MANIFEST.yaml` (`:418-422`), because over every tracked path it would fail 41 tracked documents and tests of the nine repos (each `ENFORCEMENT.md`, most `README.md` files, and `tests/Skills.Tests.ps1`, architecture 8.4); the tracked-tree run is not a step of the sync: it runs at HostPluginAdoption's exit, after that change removes the TypeScript hosts' TypeScript logic, Jest suites, and vendored Node core, while the sync runs the packaged-path check on each repo it writes (architecture 4.4 and 8.5) (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."); AC-006 the cache guard `HasOpenPluginTurn` (`:666,692-726`), which today scans only `current-turn.yaml` files for `status: in_progress`, also treats a cache as holding an open turn when any `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml` under it lists a request in `openDelivered` (the per-host-session store of architecture 3.4 and 4.1), so `ReplacePluginCache` retains that cache in both cases (architecture 8.4, BuildTooling churn). Evidence, in the Build.Tests infrastructure step of BuildTooling (A9's sync scope): `SyncAgentPluginsExplicitVersionTests`, `SyncAgentPluginsTypeScriptHostsReceiveLibPsTests` (which also asserts that the sync makes no pack or vendor call), `SyncAgentPluginsHostNameTests`, `SyncAgentPluginsReceiptMixedVersionsOrHashFailsGate`, `SyncAgentPluginsParentResolutionTests`, `SyncAgentPluginsLockfileViaNpmTests` (with the rewritten `PlanPluginVersionUpdates_BumpsMinorAndSkipsNodeModules`, Test churn), `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnlyAllPathsIncludingTestsAdapterEntryOnlyTests`, `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnlyCompiledAdapterOutputAllowed`, `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnlyExtraNodeHelperSourceFails`, `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnlyExtraDistFileFails`, `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnlyContentRulePackagedPathsOnly` (named here: a tracked document or test naming bash passes, a packaged file naming bash fails), `SyncAgentPluginsRunsPackagedPathCheckNotTrackedTreeCheck` (named here), `ReplacePluginCache_OpenTurn_RetainsExistingCache` (existing, re-seeded per host session), and `ReplacePluginCacheLegacyCurrentTurnInProgressRetainsExistingCache` (named here: the legacy-file seed the existing case carries today). [A9; BuildTooling]
